cat > docs/superpowers/specs/17-e2e-lighthouse.md <<'EOF'
# 17 · Playwright smoke + Lighthouse CI — spec

Issue: [PV3-22](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-22) · Branch: `feat/17-e2e-lighthouse`
Design: design doc §6, §9 · `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §13

## Goal

The end-to-end safety net, plus the performance budget. Small on purpose: 304 unit tests
already cover every formula, so this block only has to prove the DOM plumbing runs in a
real browser.

## Context

`bun test` covers content, i18n, all the motion math, contrast and the a11y invariants.
None of it opens a browser. Every block so far verified its own DOM work by running
shipped scripts against hand-written stubs — which is honest, but not the same as a
browser.

Two things are still unverified for exactly that reason:

- Whether the focus ring is **visually unclipped**. `overflow: hidden` on `.row`,
  `.preview` and `.edge` could crop a 2px offset ring on an element sitting flush
  against them. Issue 16 flagged this and could not close it.
- Whether the frame budget holds on a throttled machine rather than an M4.

CI today runs lint, test and build on Bun 1.4.0.

## Scope

### 1. Playwright

`bun add -d @playwright/test`. This is the one dependency this block adds, and it is
justified: nothing else drives a real browser.

`playwright.config.ts`: Chromium only, `webServer` running `bun run preview` against the
static build, `baseURL` from it, retries 0 locally and 1 in CI, trace on first retry.

### 2. The six smoke tests — `e2e/smoke.spec.ts`

Each asserts something a unit test structurally cannot:

1. **The hero boots.** After the boot sequence, the `h1` and all five `[data-boot]`
   elements are at opacity 1. Guards the whole `boot.ts` timeline in a real event loop.
2. **The theme toggle round-trips.** Click, assert `documentElement.dataset.theme` and
   `style.colorScheme` both flipped, reload, assert it persisted.
3. **The language toggle navigates.** Click, land on `/en`, assert `<html lang="en">` and
   that the `h1` matches `content.en.h1a`.
4. **A reveal fires on scroll.** A card below the fold starts at opacity 0 and reaches 1
   after scrolling to it.
5. **The method sticky advances.** Scroll through the 280vh track and assert the active
   step index goes 0 → 4 and the indicator text tracks it.
6. **`reduce` mounts no canvas.** With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` emulated:
   `page.locator('canvas')` has count 0, and the hero text is visible from the first
   frame.

Plus the one issue 16 could not do:

7. **The focus ring is not clipped.** Tab to each interactive element and assert its
   `getBoundingClientRect`, expanded by the 2px ring and its 2px offset, is inside the
   client rect of every `overflow: hidden` ancestor. If an element fails, fix the CSS —
   do not delete the assertion.

Keep it at these seven. A large E2E suite is slow and flaky, and this one exists to catch
what unit tests cannot reach, not to re-cover them.

### 3. Lighthouse CI

`bun add -d @lhci/cli`. Mobile preset against the static build.

Thresholds, all **error** level: Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices and SEO each
≥ 90.

If Performance misses, degrade in the order `MOTION_SPEC` §13 fixes — shimmer, then
aurora, then node count — and **write down in the PR what was degraded and the before/after
numbers**. Do not lower the threshold, and do not degrade preemptively: measure first.

### 4. CI wiring

Extend `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: the existing `check` job stays as is, and a second job
runs the build once, then Playwright and Lighthouse against it. Cache the Playwright
browser download.

Total CI time must stay under 5 minutes. Report the actual number.

### 5. Scripts

Add `test:e2e` (`playwright test`) and `test:lh` (`lhci autorun`). `tests/scaffold.test.ts`
asserts the exact set of package scripts, so it needs updating — that is expected, not a
reason to avoid adding them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The seven Playwright tests pass locally three runs in a row with no flake.
- [ ] They pass in CI.
- [ ] Lighthouse reports ≥ 90 on all four categories, mobile, against the built site.
- [ ] The focus-ring test genuinely fails when a ring is clipped — prove it by temporarily narrowing an ancestor, then revert.
- [ ] `bun run lint`, `bun test` and `bun run build` still pass; the scaffold script test is updated.
- [ ] Total CI wall time under 5 minutes.

## Out of scope

Visual regression snapshots. Cross-browser runs — Chromium only; the design targets
evergreen browsers and a second engine doubles CI time for little here. Deploy (issue 18).
EOF

**It found no defect** — all 21 focusable elements clear every `overflow: hidden` ancestor. I verified the test isn't vacuous before trusting that: instrumented, it visits all 21 elements, every one reports `grow=4` (2px ring + 2px offset) and `:focus-visible` matching, and 4 of them (contact email + 3 pills) sit inside 2 clipping ancestors.

```
"a.email "hi@marcosarrieta.dev↗" — ring clipped on left, top by div.reach"
"a.pill font-mono "GITHUB" — ring clipped on left, bottom by div.reach"
"a.pill font-mono "LINKEDIN" — ring clipped on bottom by div.reach"
"a.pill font-mono "TELEGRAM" — ring clipped on bottom by div.reach"
```

| Page | Performance | Accessibility | Best Practices | SEO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/index.html` | **0.99** | 0.96 | **0.96** | **1.00** |

The `/` vs `/en` gap is not a page difference — the two are byte-identical in their embeds. It is third-party CDN warmth: `/en` runs second, the CDNs are warm, more of their content lands inside the trace window. **This budget is inherently non-deterministic while the previews are live iframes**, and CI (cold, single-shot) could land anywhere.

Two paths, both needing your call: (a) convert the previews to static screenshots — design doc §8 already treats `screenshot` as a first-class mode and 2 of 6 projects use it; the PNGs are listed as pending from you in §12; or (b) accept a scoped budget that excludes third-party content, which no LHCI flag currently expresses cleanly.

1. **One component change, isolated in its own commit (`71a36bd`) so you can revert it alone.** This is the one place I went past "don't touch components". The Projects markup already promised *"never loaded before it is scrolled to"* and `loading="lazy"` did not deliver: measured under Pixel 5 emulation, **50 external requests fire with zero scrolling**, 5700px before the section. `data-src` + a small IntersectionObserver → **0 before, 4 iframes after scrolling**. It took the ES page from 0.74–0.82/0.79 to 0.99/0.96. I judged it a genuine defect against documented intent rather than test-gaming — but it does not make the budget pass, so if you'd rather it be its own issue, revert that one commit.
2. **`bunfig.toml` with `[test] root = "tests"`.** Bun's default patterns match `*.spec.ts`, so `bun test` was picking up `e2e/smoke.spec.ts` and failing. Verified: 304 pass either way.
3. **`webServer.env: { ASTRO_PREVIEW_BACKGROUND: 'false' }`.** Astro 7 auto-daemonizes `preview` when it detects a coding-agent environment; Playwright reads the foreground exit as the server dying. Not needed in CI, harmless there.
4. **Node-ESM JSON import.** `e2e/` runs under Node, so it needs `import content from '../handoff/content.json' with { type: 'json' }` (default export only), unlike `src/lib/content.ts` which Vite resolves.
5. **Test 1 asserts *every* `[data-boot]` element**, not "five" — there are six (hero 0–4 plus console at 10).

## CI wall time

Measured locally, warm: install 0.07s, lint 3.0s, unit tests 0.8s, build 0.5s, Playwright 5.3s, **Lighthouse 78s**. The two jobs run in parallel, so the critical path is the `browser` job: **~85s of work**, plus GitHub runner setup and a cold `bun install` — comfortably under the 5-minute budget. Lighthouse is 90% of it; dropping `numberOfRuns` to 1 would cut it to ~26s if that ever matters.</result>

It is third-party CDN warmth: `/en` runs second, the CDNs are warm, more of their content lands inside the trace window. **This budget is inherently non-deterministic while the previews are live iframes**, and CI (cold, single-shot) could land anywhere.

Two paths, both needing your call: (a) convert the previews to static screenshots — design doc §8 already treats `screenshot` as a first-class mode and 2 of 6 projects use it; the PNGs are listed as pending from you in §12; or (b) accept a scoped budget that excludes third-party content, which no LHCI flag currently expresses cleanly.

1. **One component change, isolated in its own commit (`71a36bd`) so you can revert it alone.** This is the one place I went past "don't touch components". The Projects markup already promised *"never loaded before it is scrolled to"* and `loading="lazy"` did not deliver: measured under Pixel 5 emulation, **50 external requests fire with zero scrolling**, 5700px before the section. `data-src` + a small IntersectionObserver → **0 before, 4 iframes after scrolling**. It took the ES page from 0.74–0.82/0.79 to 0.99/0.96. I judged it a genuine defect against documented intent rather than test-gaming — but it does not make the budget pass, so if you'd rather it be its own issue, revert that one commit.

3. **`webServer.env: { ASTRO_PREVIEW_BACKGROUND: 'false' }`.** Astro 7 auto-daemonizes `preview` when it detects a coding-agent environment; Playwright reads the foreground exit as the server dying. Not needed in CI, harmless there.
4. **Node-ESM JSON import.** `e2e/` runs under Node, so it needs `import content from '../handoff/content.json' with { type: 'json' }` (default export only), unlike `src/lib/content.ts` which Vite resolves.

Measured locally, warm: install 0.07s, lint 3.0s, unit tests 0.8s, build 0.5s, Playwright 5.3s, **Lighthouse 78s**. The two jobs run in parallel, so the critical path is the `browser` job: **~85s of work**, plus GitHub runner setup and a cold `bun install` — comfortably under the 5-minute budget. content.text:
Verificado: 7 tests pasan en 5.4s, y los iframes ahora salen con `data-src`.

Dos cosas antes de la PR — una que el agente arregló bien, y una decisión que es tuya.

**El arreglo:** el markup de Proyectos prometía en su propio comentario que los iframes *"nunca cargan antes de scrollear hasta ellos"*, y `loading="lazy"` no lo cumplía. Medido con emulación de Pixel 5: **50 requests externos salían sin scrollear nada**, con la sección a 5700px de distancia. Chrome aplica `lazy` con un margen enorme en conexiones rápidas. Ahora es `data-src` + IntersectionObserver: 0 antes, 4 después. Eso solo llevó la página ES de 0.74 a 0.99 en Performance.

**La decisión:** con los previews en vivo, el presupuesto de Lighthouse **no puede pasar de forma determinista**.

| Página | Perf | A11y | Best Practices | SEO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | 0.99 | 0.96 | 0.96 | 1.00 |
| `/en` | **0.82** ✘ | 0.96 | **0.79** ✘ | 1.00 |

El sitio propio está impecable: quitando los iframes del build, ambas páginas dan **1.00 / 0.96 / 1.00 / 1.00**. Todo el déficit son los cuatro embeds en vivo, que arrastran 40–50 requests de terceros — Tag Manager, Wix, Cloudflare Insights — más las penalizaciones por cookies de terceros. La diferencia entre `/` y `/en` no es de la página: son idénticas. Es que `/en` corre segunda, con los CDN ya calientes, y entra más contenido ajeno en la ventana de medición. En CI, en frío y de una sola pasada, puede caer en cualquier lado.

El agente hizo lo correcto: midió antes de degradar, comprobó que shimmer, aurora y nodos no tienen nada que ver (TBT 0ms, CLS 0.005), y **no tocó el diseño ni bajó el umbral**.

// How each project is previewed. Declarative and keyed by **host**, never by position
// in `content.json`: reordering the list must not change what a given site renders as,
// which is exactly what an index-keyed table would do.
//
// All six are screenshots (`public/previews/<host>.png`, regenerated by
// `scripts/capture-previews.ts`). Two of them always were — `creativamedialab.com`
// answers `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `telecentro.com.ar` sits behind a WAF — and the
// other four moved here for the budget of spec 17: four live cross-origin iframes pull
// 40-50 third-party requests into the page, which cost `/en` Performance 0.82 and Best
// Practices 0.79. Static images, both pages score 1.00.

export type PreviewMode = 'screenshot'

export const PREVIEWS: Record<string, PreviewMode> = {
  'nera-agro.com': 'screenshot',
  'agropro.ag': 'screenshot',
  'kodaiverse.com': 'screenshot',
  'masushuaia.com': 'screenshot',
  'creativamedialab.com': 'screenshot',
  'telecentro.com.ar': 'screenshot',
}

/**
 * A host nobody declared still gets a screenshot, so a project added to `content.json`
 * without its PNG falls back to the striped placeholder rather than to nothing. The
 * unit test is what keeps it from staying undeclared.
 */
export function previewMode(host: string): PreviewMode {
  return PREVIEWS[host] ?? 'screenshot'
}

Closes PV3-22.

The end-to-end safety net and the performance budget. Small on purpose — 305 unit tests already cover every formula, the contrast ratios and the a11y invariants, so this block only proves the DOM plumbing runs in a real browser.

## Verification

```
bun run lint      → passes
bun test          → 305 pass, 0 fail
bun run build     → 2 pages built
bunx playwright   → 7 passed (5.5s), three consecutive runs, no flake
```

**Lighthouse, mobile, 3 runs per page, both routes:**

| | Performance | Accessibility | Best Practices | SEO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | **1.00** | 0.96 | **1.00** | **1.00** |
| `/en` | **1.00** | 0.96 | **1.00** | **1.00** |

## The focus-ring test closes issue 16's open item

Issue 16 could not verify whether the ring is *visually* clipped — that is layout geometry, not structure, and it needs a browser. Test 7 tabs to all 21 focusable elements, expands each rect by the 2px ring plus its 2px offset, and asserts it fits inside every `overflow: hidden` ancestor.

**It found no defect.** More importantly, it was proven to bite: adding `overflow: hidden` to Contact's `.reach` — whose padding box is flush with the email — made it fail with four named elements, *while the elements themselves still fit*. Only the ring crossed the boundary, which is the exact defect class. Reverted, green again. A test that cannot fail is worse than no test.

## Two real defects fixed along the way

**`loading="lazy"` was not deferring anything.** The Projects markup promised in its own comment that iframes never load before being scrolled to. Measured under Pixel 5 emulation: 50 external requests fired with zero scrolling, with the section 5700px away. Chrome applies a large margin on fast connections.

**The previews are now static screenshots** — all six, your call after I laid out the tradeoff. Four live cross-origin embeds dragged 40–50 third-party requests into the page (Tag Manager, Wix, Cloudflare Insights) plus third-party-cookie penalties, costing `/en` Performance 0.82 and Best Practices 0.79. Worse, the `/` vs `/en` gap was not a page difference — the pages are identical — but CDN warmth, which made the budget non-deterministic and would have landed anywhere in cold CI.

The agent measured before touching anything and correctly refused to degrade shimmer, aurora or node count: TBT was 0ms and CLS 0.005, so `MOTION_SPEC` §13's levers would have hurt the design for zero gain. It also refused to lower a threshold.

JPEG rather than PNG: **723 KB across the six against 2.5 MB**, same 960×660 pixels. The iframe path and its `IntersectionObserver` are gone rather than left as dead code, and three tests that asserted iframe behavior were rewritten — including one that now guards against an iframe quietly coming back.

## Known, not a defect

Accessibility sits at 0.96 on both pages, above the 90 threshold. The single failing audit is `color-contrast` on the Method section's **upcoming** step cards, which sit at `opacity: .22` by design (`MOTION_SPEC` §7). Lighthouse measures a static snapshot at load; those cards light up as you scroll, and with `reduce` or with JavaScript disabled they are never dimmed at all. Raising the opacity would contradict the motion spec, so it stays documented rather than "fixed".

## Notes

- **CI**: two jobs in parallel; the critical path is the browser job at ~85s of work plus runner setup. Lighthouse is 90% of it. Comfortably under the 5-minute budget.
- `bunfig.toml` pins `[test] root = "tests"` — Bun's default patterns were picking up `e2e/smoke.spec.ts` and failing it.
- `webServer.env` sets `ASTRO_PREVIEW_BACKGROUND=false`: Astro 7 auto-daemonizes `preview` in agent environments, and Playwright reads the foreground exit as the server dying.
- Two dependencies added, both expected: `@playwright/test` and `@lhci/cli`.

python3 - <<'PY'
import json, pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('lighthouserc.json')
c = json.loads(p.read_text())
c['ci']['collect']['settings'] = {
    # GitHub's Ubuntu runners restrict unprivileged user namespaces through AppArmor, so
    # Chrome's sandbox cannot start and the launcher dies with "No usable sandbox!".
    # Playwright passes its own flags and is unaffected; Lighthouse launches Chrome
    # itself, so it needs them here. Safe on an ephemeral runner loading only our build.
    'chromeFlags': '--no-sandbox --disable-dev-shm-usage',
}
p.write_text(json.dumps(c, indent=2) + '\n')
PY
bun run format >/dev/null 2>&1; cat lighthouserc.json | head -12; bunx lhci autorun 2>&1 | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | tail -3

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   The user (Marcos Arrieta, `marcosarrietaarg@gmail.com`) asked to build his personal portfolio site `marcosarrieta.dev` from a design handoff produced by Claude Design. Explicit requests, in order:
   - Create the GitHub repo (already existed as `djmaam/portfolio-v3`).
   - Read ALL the handoff documentation and build from it. Stack: Bun + Astro + whatever libraries are needed.
   - **Work scheme must be SDD (Spec-Driven Development) + TDD.** Create issues in Linear in workspace **Portfolio-djmaam-v3**, generate a spec per task, and **I decide which subagent executes each one and orchestrate the development**.
   - Font decision: **Manrope** (over Geist).
   - Logos: create the task but **do not define anything yet — leave it to plan later**.
   - Later: "vamos con la ultima version de todo, asi lo tenemos lo mas actualizado posible" (latest version of every dependency).
   - `.DS_Store` must not be in the repo, and `.gitignore` must prevent recurrence.
   - **"la idea es que todo el proyecto este en ingles para mejorar la legilibidad de agentes y personas"** — all code comments, then all specs and Linear issues, translated to English.
   - **"seria bueno actualizarlo a ingles americano porque es el que entiendo y hablo"** — American English spelling specifically.
   - Run two, then four blocks in parallel when they don't collide.
   - Resolve merge conflicts on PRs #12, #13, #14 when they arose.
   - Check the GitHub↔Linear integration (user couldn't connect the new workspace).
   - When Lighthouse couldn't pass deterministically with live iframes, chose **"Screenshots estáticos"** for all six project previews.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - Astro 7.3.1 static output, Bun 1.4.0 (runtime, package manager, test runner), TypeScript strict (pinned ^6.0.3), Tailwind v4.3.3 via `@tailwindcss/vite`.
   - `@theme static` in Tailwind v4 (needed so unused tokens still emit), `light-dark()` CSS function, `color-mix()` for one-off alphas (Tailwind opacity modifiers do NOT work on `light-dark()` colors).
   - SDD + TDD: one Linear issue = one block = one branch `feat/NN-<block>` = one PR; spec written and committed before code; acceptance criteria are the tests.
   - Motion math extracted to pure functions in `src/lib/motion/math.ts`, unit-tested without a DOM, so Playwright stays small.
   - Single scroll listener for the whole site (`src/lib/motion/scroll.ts`) with a subscriber API (`onScroll`); guarded by tests.
   - Progressive enhancement: `html.has-js` gates all `opacity: 0` resting states; `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` gates all animation.
   - Marker-based parallel work: `// section-import: <name>` and `{/* section: <name> */}` lines in both page files so parallel branches replace distinct lines.
   - Git worktree isolation for parallel subagents.
   - WCAG 2.1 relative luminance computed in a unit test from parsed CSS tokens.
   - Lighthouse CI with mobile preset, four categories at ≥ 0.90, error level.

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   - **`CLAUDE.md`** (root, created by me) — the root-cause fix for the language convention; it's what subagents read first. Key section:
     ```markdown
     ## Language

     **Everything is written in American English** — code comments, identifiers, commit
     messages, script output, test names, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and the specs under
     `docs/superpowers/specs/`. This applies to code written by subagents too. Watch the
     easy slips: `color` not `colour`, `math` not `maths`, `behavior` not `behaviour`,
     `normalize` not `normalise`.

     The only exception is `handoff/`, which stays in Spanish on purpose: it is the
     read-only design source of truth, and `handoff/content.json` holds the site copy in
     Spanish and English (that is product content, not code).
     ```
     Also documents: no literal colors outside `src/styles/app.css`, no hardcoded copy, motion math in pure functions, one scroll listener, reduced-motion, `has-js`.

   - **`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-portfolio-v3-design.md`** — the technical design doc. Records Astro 7 (not 5), Manrope + IBM Plex Mono (no variable version of the mono exists on Google Fonts), no UI framework in v1 (React only as a single island for the v1.1 agent console), and §8 (rewritten in the last block) now says all six previews are static JPEG screenshots.

   - **`docs/superpowers/specs/NN-<block>.md`** — 00-scaffold, 01-tokens-tema, 02-content-i18n, 03-base-layout, 04-nav, 05-hero, 06-console, 07-network-canvas, 08-about, 09-method, 10-experience, 11-projects, 12-stack, 13-contact, 14-footer, 16-a11y, 17-e2e-lighthouse. All in English.

   - **`src/lib/content.ts`** — single content source, types derived from JSON:
     ```ts
     import raw from '../../handoff/content.json'
     export type Lang = 'es' | 'en'
     export type Content = (typeof raw)['i18n']['es']
     export const LANGS = ['es', 'en'] as const satisfies readonly Lang[]
     export const site = { name: 'Marcos Arrieta', handle: '@djmaam' } as const
     export const content: Record<Lang, Content> = raw.i18n
     export const { links, stack, consoleLog } = raw
     ```

   - **`src/lib/ui.ts`** — UI chrome that `content.json` (read-only) has no key for: `ui.es/en.themeToggle`, `ui.*.skipToContent`, `stats = { years: '8+', companies: '5', platforms: '6' }`, `consoleChrome`, and `alsoWithCompanies = ['Creativa Media Lab', 'Kodai', 'Hashme', 'Demedis'] as const` (sourced from the mock at `Portfolio.dc.html:697`).

   - **`src/lib/projects.ts`** — preview modes keyed by **host, never by index**:
     ```ts
     export type PreviewMode = 'screenshot'
     export const PREVIEWS: Record<string, PreviewMode> = {
       'nera-agro.com': 'screenshot', 'agropro.ag': 'screenshot',
       'kodaiverse.com': 'screenshot', 'masushuaia.com': 'screenshot',
       'creativamedialab.com': 'screenshot', 'telecentro.com.ar': 'screenshot',
     }
     export function previewMode(host: string): PreviewMode { return PREVIEWS[host] ?? 'screenshot' }
     ```

   - **`src/lib/motion/math.ts`** — ~25 pure functions: `auroraStyle`, `docProgress`, `scrambleFrame(target, p, rand = Math.random)`, `anchorOffset`, `bootDelay(n) = 500 + n*170`, `typedLength`, `metricsAt(tick)` (`agents = 3 + tick%2`, `specs = 12 + ⌊tick/11⌋`, `shipped = 41 + ⌊tick/6⌋`), `logWindow`, `wordOpacity`, `aboutProgress`, `revealDelay`, `methodStep`, `methodCardState`, `methodProgress`, `methodLabel`, plus 19 canvas functions (`ellipsoidPoint`, `projectNode`, `asteriskTarget`, `formationPhase`, `connectionAlpha`, `collapseFactor`, `commandHopDelay`, `nodeCountFor`, etc.).

   - **`src/styles/app.css`** — all tokens in `@theme static` with `light-dark()`; 11 keyframes; `@utility container-page/section-y/section-divider`; `--nav-h: 64px`; global `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent); outline-offset: 2px }`; `scroll-margin-top`/`scroll-padding-top: var(--nav-h)`; `--color-contact-accent: light-dark(#087a95, #0a8faf)` (darkened in issue 16 from `#3ee7ff` for contrast).

   - **`scripts/check-tokens.ts`** — the anti-hex lint, run from `bun run lint`. Note: it scans comments too.

   - **`lighthouserc.json`** — most recent edit, the CI fix:
     ```json
     "collect": {
       "staticDistDir": "./dist",
       "numberOfRuns": 3,
       "settings": { "chromeFlags": "--no-sandbox --disable-dev-shm-usage" }
     }
     ```

   - **`scripts/capture-previews.ts`** — regenerates the six screenshots with Playwright; viewport 1440×990, `deviceScaleFactor: 2/3`, dismisses consent banners, waits 4s for entrance animations, writes `public/previews/<host>.jpg` at `quality: 82`.

   - **`e2e/smoke.spec.ts`** — 7 Playwright tests: hero boots, theme toggle round-trips, language toggle navigates, reveal fires on scroll, method sticky advances 0→4, `reduce` mounts no canvas, and **the focus ring is never clipped by an overflow ancestor**.

4. **Errors and fixes:**

   - **`git reset --hard` ran on `main`**: the `git checkout -q feat/08-about` failed ("branch already exists"), so the chained `git reset --hard origin/feat/08-about` moved local `main` to the About commit. Fixed with `git branch -f main origin/main`; `origin/main` was untouched and the specs commit survived in both feature branches. I stated this plainly as my error.
   - **Reported green on a red test**: I verified with `bun test 2>&1 | tail -2`, which cut off the `1 fail` line. CI caught it. Switched to `tail -4` and told the subagents to read the full summary.
   - **False lint failure from agent worktrees**: `.claude/worktrees/*` each carry a `tsconfig.json`, so typescript-eslint refused to parse anything ("multiple candidate TSConfigRootDirs"). Fixed by adding `.claude/` to `eslint.config.js` ignores and `.prettierignore`.
   - **Sibling-marker test coupling** (3 occurrences): `experience.test.ts`, `stack.test.ts`, `contact.test.ts` each asserted the *other* sections' markers still exist — a transient state that broke on every sibling merge. All three rewritten to assert only their own marker. This was induced by my own spec wording ("don't touch the other markers").
   - **Merge conflicts on PR #12, #13, #14**: markers on adjacent lines merge as one hunk. Resolved mechanically each time, keeping both sides in design order.
   - **`content.json` not tree-shakeable**: importing `consoleLog` into a client module pulled the whole file (5.9 kB gz vs 0.5 kB). Fixed with `json: { stringify: false }` in `astro.config.mjs` + named imports.
   - **`loading="lazy"` didn't defer iframes**: 50 external requests fired with zero scrolling. Fixed with `data-src` + IntersectionObserver (later removed entirely when previews became screenshots).
   - **Lighthouse "No usable sandbox!" in CI**: GitHub's Ubuntu runners restrict unprivileged user namespaces via AppArmor. Playwright passes its own flags; LHCI launches Chrome itself. Fixed with `chromeFlags: "--no-sandbox --disable-dev-shm-usage"`.
   - **PNG previews weighed 2.5 MB**: converted to JPEG q82 via macOS `sips` → 723 KB; `cwebp`/`magick` unavailable, `sips` webp produced no output.
   - **British spelling slipped in** ("maths") despite CLAUDE.md: fixed the files, left the commit subject, and added explicit examples of the easy slips to CLAUDE.md.

5. **Problem Solving:**

   Solved: the mock is a dc-runtime React-like component (math portable, plumbing/CSS not); IBM Plex Mono has no variable version; Tailwind opacity modifiers don't work on `light-dark()`; canvas can't read `--color-accent` directly (returns unresolved `light-dark()`), so the element carries `color: var(--color-accent)` and the class reads `styles.color` back; console timestamps must be client-side (a static build would freeze one clock forever) while the footer's year is correctly build-time; `aria-live="off"` not `polite` for a decorative auto-cycling log; the contact card inverts the theme so it needs its own accent token; a stylesheet cannot override an inline custom property (hence the `--step`/`--lit` indirection in Method); Lighthouse's 0.96 accessibility is a single `color-contrast` audit on Method's intentionally-dimmed upcoming cards (`opacity: .22` per MOTION_SPEC §7) — documented, not "fixed".

   Ongoing/open: the GitHub↔Linear integration (user was told to check `https://github.com/settings/installations`; it now works — issues receive PR attachments); `public/previews` PNGs are now generated so that pending item is closed; company logos (issue 15) still undefined.

# RTK - Rust Token Killer

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (cuts up to 90% of bash output)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
which rtk             # Verify correct binary
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

## Hook-Based Usage

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.
Example: `git status` → `rtk git status` (transparent, 0 tokens overhead)

Refer to CLAUDE.md for full command reference.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. ## codegraph
# Codegraph — available (per-project; pass projectPath)

Codegraph is a SQLite knowledge graph of a codebase's symbols, edges, and
files: one `codegraph_explore` call returns the verbatim, line-numbered source
of the relevant symbols PLUS the call paths between them and a blast-radius
summary — replacing a grep + Read loop with one round-trip.

This server started somewhere with no `.codegraph/` of its own, so there is no
default project — but the tools are available and work **per project**:

- To query a project that HAS a `.codegraph/` index (e.g. a service inside a
  monorepo, or a second repo), pass its path as `projectPath` to
  `codegraph_explore` (and any other codegraph tool). Codegraph resolves the
  nearest `.codegraph/` at or above that path and answers from it — for as many
  projects as you like in one session.
- For a project with no `.codegraph/`, use your built-in tools (Read/Grep/Glob)
  for that project. Indexing is the user's decision — don't run it yourself, but
  if it comes up they can run `codegraph init` in a project to enable codegraph
  there (a new index is picked up live, no restart).


---
CodeGraph v1.6.0 is available (this server is running v1.5.0). Update with `codegraph upgrade`. This server keeps running the old version until the user upgrades — mention it when convenient; do not run the upgrade yourself.

Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

PONYTAIL MODE ACTIVE — level: full

# Ponytail

You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. You have
seen every over-engineered codebase and been paged at 3am for one. The best
code is the code never written.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No drift back to over-building. Still active if
unsure. Off only: "stop ponytail" / "normal mode". Default: **full**.
Switch: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.

## The ladder

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it, say so in one line. (YAGNI)
2. **Already in this codebase?** A helper, util, type, or pattern that already lives here → reuse it. Look before you write; re-implementing what's a few files over is the most common slop.
3. **Stdlib does it?** Use it.
4. **Native platform feature covers it?** `<input type="date">` over a picker lib, CSS over JS, DB constraint over app code.
5. **Already-installed dependency solves it?** Use it. Never add a new one for what a few lines can do.
6. **Can it be one line?** One line.
7. **Only then:** the minimum code that works.

The ladder is a reflex, not a research project — but it runs *after* you
understand the problem, not instead of it. Read the task and the code it
touches first, trace the real flow end to end, then climb. Two rungs work →
take the higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the
right one — once you actually know what the change has to touch.

**Bug fix = root cause, not symptom.** A report names a symptom. Before you
edit, grep every caller of the function you're about to touch. The lazy fix IS
the root-cause fix: one guard in the shared function is a smaller diff than a
guard in every caller — and patching only the path the ticket names leaves
every sibling caller still broken. Fix it once, where all callers route through.

## Rules

- No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
- No boilerplate, no scaffolding "for later", later can scaffold for itself.
- Deletion over addition. Boring over clever, clever is what someone decodes at 3am.
- Fewest files possible. Shortest working diff wins — but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
- Complex request? Ship the lazy version and question it in the same response, "Did X; Y covers it. Need full X? Say so." Never stall on an answer you can default.
- Two stdlib options, same size? Take the one that's correct on edge cases. Lazy means writing less code, not picking the flimsier algorithm.
- Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path (`# ponytail: global lock, per-account locks if throughput matters`).

## Output

Code first. Then at most three short lines: what was skipped, when to add it.
No essays, no feature tours, no design notes. If the explanation is longer
than the code, delete the explanation, every paragraph defending a
simplification is complexity smuggled back in as prose. Explanation the user
explicitly asked for (a report, a walkthrough, per-phase notes) is not debt,
give it in full, the rule is only against unrequested prose.

Pattern: `[code] → skipped: [X], add when [Y].`

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | The ladder enforced. Stdlib and native first. Shortest diff, shortest explanation. Default. |

Example: "Add a cache for these API responses."
- full: "`@lru_cache(maxsize=1000)` on the fetch function. Skipped custom cache class, add when lru_cache measurably falls short."

## When NOT to be lazy

Never simplify away: input validation at trust boundaries, error handling
that prevents data loss, security measures, accessibility basics, anything
explicitly requested. User insists on the full version → build it, no
re-arguing.

Never lazy about understanding the problem. The ladder shortens the
solution, never the reading. Trace the whole thing first — every file the
change touches, the actual flow — before picking a rung. Laziness that skips
comprehension to ship a small diff is the dangerous kind: it dresses up as
efficiency and ships a confident wrong fix. Read fully, then be lazy.

Hardware is never the ideal on paper: a real clock drifts, a real sensor
reads off, a PCA9685 runs a few percent fast. Leave the calibration knob, not
just less code, the physical world needs tuning a minimal model can't see.

Lazy code without its check is unfinished. Non-trivial logic (a branch, a
loop, a parser, a money/security path) leaves ONE runnable check behind, the
smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks: an `assert`-based
`demo()`/`__main__` self-check or one small `test_*.py`. No frameworks, no
fixtures, no per-function suites unless asked. Trivial one-liners need no
test, YAGNI applies to tests too.

## Boundaries

Ponytail governs what you build, not how you talk (pair with Caveman for
terse prose). "stop ponytail" / "normal mode": revert. Level persists until
changed or session end.

The shortest path to done is the right path.

5. **Already-installed dependency solves it?** Use it. Never add a new one for what a few lines can do.
6. **Can it be one line?** One line.
7. **Only then:** the minimum code that works.

The ladder is a reflex, not a research project — but it runs *after* you
understand the problem, not instead of it. Read the task and the code it
touches first, trace the real flow end to end, then climb. Two rungs work →
take the higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the
right one — once you actually know what the change has to touch.

**Bug fix = root cause, not symptom.** A report names a symptom. Before you
edit, grep every caller of the function you're about to touch. The lazy fix IS
the root-cause fix: one guard in the shared function is a smaller diff than a
guard in every caller — and patching only the path the ticket names leaves
every sibling caller still broken. Fix it once, where all callers route through.

## Rules

- No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
- No boilerplate, no scaffolding "for later", later can scaffold for itself.
- Deletion over addition. Boring over clever, clever is what someone decodes at 3am.
- Fewest files possible. Shortest working diff wins — but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
- Complex request? Ship the lazy version and question it in the same response, "Did X; Y covers it. Need full X? Say so." Never stall on an answer you can default.
- Two stdlib options, same size? Take the one that's correct on edge cases. Lazy means writing less code, not picking the flimsier algorithm.
- Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path (`# ponytail: global lock, per-account locks if throughput matters`).

## Output

Code first. Then at most three short lines: what was skipped, when to add it.
No essays, no feature tours, no design notes. If the explanation is longer
than the code, delete the explanation, every paragraph defending a
simplification is complexity smuggled back in as prose. Explanation the user
explicitly asked for (a report, a walkthrough, per-phase notes) is not debt,
give it in full, the rule is only against unrequested prose.

Pattern: `[code] → skipped: [X], add when [Y].`

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | The ladder enforced. Stdlib and native first. Shortest diff, shortest explanation. Default. |

Example: "Add a cache for these API responses."
- full: "`@lru_cache(maxsize=1000)` on the fetch function. Skipped custom cache class, add when lru_cache measurably falls short."

## When NOT to be lazy

Never simplify away: input validation at trust boundaries, error handling
that prevents data loss, security measures, accessibility basics, anything
explicitly requested. User insists on the full version → build it, no
re-arguing.

Never lazy about understanding the problem. The ladder shortens the
solution, never the reading. Trace the whole thing first — every file the
change touches, the actual flow — before picking a rung. Laziness that skips
comprehension to ship a small diff is the dangerous kind: it dresses up as
efficiency and ships a confident wrong fix. Read fully, then be lazy.

Hardware is never the ideal on paper: a real clock drifts, a real sensor
reads off, a PCA9685 runs a few percent fast. Leave the calibration knob, not
just less code, the physical world needs tuning a minimal model can't see.

Lazy code without its check is unfinished. Non-trivial logic (a branch, a
loop, a parser, a money/security path) leaves ONE runnable check behind, the
smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks: an `assert`-based
`demo()`/`__main__` self-check or one small `test_*.py`. No frameworks, no
fixtures, no per-function suites unless asked. Trivial one-liners need no
test, YAGNI applies to tests too.

## Boundaries

Ponytail governs what you build, not how you talk (pair with Caveman for
terse prose). "stop ponytail" / "normal mode": revert. Level persists until
changed or session end.

The shortest path to done is the right path.

# DESIGN_SPEC — Portfolio v3

Referencia viva: `reference/Portfolio.dc.html`. Los valores de abajo son los del mock.

## 1. Identidad

Concepto: **"Pienso el producto. Orquesto cómo se construye."** Mezcla 50/50 de lenguaje Apple (tipografía grande, aire, vidrio, radios suaves) y cyberpunk contenido (cian neón, labels mono, consola en vivo, red de nodos). Una sola familia de acento (cian) + violeta como secundario solo en interacciones (cursor de la red, haz de contacto).

## 2. Tokens

### Color (usar `light-dark(light, dark)`; el root lleva `color-scheme`)

| Token | Light | Dark | Uso |
|---|---|---|---|
| bg | `#F4F5F7` | `#08090C` | fondo de página |
| ink | `#0B0D12` | `#F3F5F9` | texto principal |
| dim | `#5E6675` | `#8B94A7` | texto secundario, labels |
| line | `rgba(0,0,0,.08)` | `rgba(255,255,255,.08)` | separadores, bordes |
| surface | `rgba(255,255,255,.7)` | `rgba(255,255,255,.035)` | tarjetas (con `border: 1px solid` line a .06/.07) |
| glass | `rgba(244,245,247,.72)` | `rgba(8,9,12,.6)` | nav (`backdrop-filter: blur(18px) saturate(1.4)`) |
| accent | `#0A8FAF` | `#3EE7FF` | cian |
| accent-soft | `rgba(10,143,175,.08)` | `rgba(62,231,255,.08)` | fondos de chips destacados |
| violet | `rgb(120,90,255)` | `rgb(170,120,255)` | solo interacciones |
| console-bg | `rgba(255,255,255,.75)` | `rgba(14,16,22,.85)` | tarjeta consola (`blur(20px)`) |
| contact-card | `#0B0D12` (invertida) | `#F3F5F9` (invertida) | la tarjeta de contacto invierte el tema |
| semáforo pasos | `#FF5C5C` `#FF9F43` `#FFD64D` `#9BE15D` `#3DDC84` | idem | dots de "Cómo trabajo" |

Glow del acento: `0 0 12px accent` en dots; `text-shadow: 0 0 40px accent@.3–.45` en la segunda línea del H1.

### Tipografía

- **Sans**: Geist (300–700). Alternativa aprobada para probar: Manrope. Fallback `-apple-system, "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif`.
- **Mono**: Geist Mono (400–500). Alternativa: IBM Plex Mono.
- Self-hosted, woff2 variable, `font-display: swap`.

Escala (fluida, con `cqw` sobre el contenedor de 1200px; en Astro usar `clamp(..., vw, ...)` equivalente):

| Rol | Tamaño | Peso | Tracking | Línea |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H1 hero | `clamp(36px, 4.9cqw, 76px)` | 600 | -.04em | 1.0, `text-wrap: balance` |
| H2 sección | `clamp(32px, 4cqw, 56px)` | 600 | -.035em | 1.02 |
| H2 stack | `clamp(32px, 4cqw, 48px)` | 600 | -.035em | 1.05 |
| H2 contacto | `clamp(34px, 4.5cqw, 64px)` | 600 | -.04em | 1.0 |
| Lead "Sobre mí" | `clamp(26px, 3cqw, 40px)` | 500 | -.025em | 1.2 |
| Sub hero | `clamp(16px, 1.3cqw, 19px)` | 400 | 0 | 1.55 |
| Body | 17px (15–18 en tarjetas) | 400 | 0 | 1.5 |
| Título tarjeta | 19–22px | 500 | -.02em | 1.15 |
| Label sección mono | 12px | 400 | .14em | — (`02 / CÓMO TRABAJO`) |
| Label mono chico | 10–11px | 400–500 | .1–.12em | — |
| Botón pill | 15px sans / 12px mono `.06em` | 500 | — | — |

### Espaciado y forma

- Contenedor: `max-width: 1200px; padding: 0 clamp(20px, 4vw, 48px)`.
- Padding vertical de sección: `clamp(56px, 7vw, 100px)`; hero `clamp(72px,10vw,140px)` arriba / `clamp(64px,8vw,110px)` abajo.
- Separador entre secciones: `border-top: 1px solid line`.
- Radios: pills `999px`; chips `8px`; tarjetas `18–24px`; consola `28px`; contacto `32px`; logos `16px`.
- Sombras: solo la consola (`0 30px 80px rgba(0,0,0,.12/.6)`) y tarjetas en hover (`0 20px 60px`).
- Grids: siempre `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, Xpx), 1fr))` con X = 380 (hero), 300 (about, stack header, proyectos), 260 (experiencia), 220 (skills), 200 (principios), 150 (pasos: 5 en una fila desde ~850px).

## 3. Estructura de página (orden)

1. **Nav** sticky, glass. Izquierda: ✳ animado + "Marcos Arrieta" (scramble). Derecha: links (Sobre mí · Experiencia · Proyectos · Contacto), toggle idioma `ES / en`, toggle tema (círculo half-fill). En mobile los links se ocultan (menú no diseñado: usar solo toggles + scroll natural, o un menú simple).
2. **Hero** 2 columnas. Izq: eyebrow mono tipeado con cursor, H1 en dos líneas (segunda en cian), sub, 2 CTAs (primario relleno ink, secundario outline), stats mono (`8+ años · 5 empresas principales · 6 plataformas`). Der: **consola** (header con 3 puntos + "orchestrator — session 0x4D41" + LIVE; log de 6 líneas `hh:mm:ss · key · value` con scanlines sutiles; footer 3 métricas AGENTS / SPECS / SHIPPED). Fondo: canvas de red de nodos (ver MOTION) + aurora fija.
3. **01 / Sobre mí**: label a la izquierda, contenido 2/3 a la derecha: lead grande (palabras que se iluminan al scroll), párrafo, 3 principios en tarjetas.
4. **02 / Cómo trabajo**: header + indicador de estado (dot + texto mono) + 5 tarjetas (número, dot, título, texto, herramienta al pie con `border-top: dashed`). Sección **pinned** en desktop (ver MOTION).
5. **03 / Experiencia**: timeline vertical: riel 1px + dot (el actual en cian con glow), logo 56px (placeholder rayado con abreviatura), empresa + período mono, rol en cian, nota, chips de alcance (mono 11px, radio 8px). Debajo, caja dashed "TAMBIÉN CON" con nombres.
6. **04 / Proyectos**: grid de tarjetas: preview 16:11 (iframe estático o screenshot) con etiqueta tipo `AGTECH · WEB + MOBILE` arriba a la izquierda y shimmer; fila inferior: nombre + descripción de una línea + `↗`. Sin stack.
7. **05 / Stack**: header + 3 filas marquesina (velocidades 70/85/78s, la del medio invertida, pausa en hover, máscara de desvanecimiento en los bordes) + leyenda `● USO A DIARIO / ○ TAMBIÉN HABLO`. Chips destacados en cian; el resto outline gris.
8. **06 / Contacto**: tarjeta invertida con grilla fluida de fondo, haz de luz cian→violeta girando en el borde (2px) + halo exterior difuso. Izq: label, H2, sub. Der: email grande subrayado con `↗`, pills GitHub / LinkedIn / Telegram con ícono monocromo (máscara sobre `currentColor`).
9. **Footer**: `© 2026 Marcos Arrieta · @djmaam` · ✳ + "Diseñado con criterio, construido con agentes." + ASCIImoji rotativo.

## 4. Estados

- Links nav: dim → ink en hover. CTA primario: `translateY(-1px)` en hover. Outline: borde → accent.
- Tarjetas hover: `translateY(-4px)`, borde accent@.45, sombra.
- Toggle idioma/tema: borde → accent en hover.
- Email: color → ink en hover, gap con la flecha crece 10→16px.
- Pills contacto: borde y texto → accent (el ícono hereda).
- Focus visible: anillo `2px accent` con offset 2px en todo lo interactivo (no está en el mock; agregarlo).

## 5. Responsive

- Todo fluido; sin breakpoints duros salvo: nav links ocultos < ~720px; "Cómo trabajo" no se fija si ancho < 720px o si el bloque no entra en la altura de la ventana.
- Hero pasa a una columna (consola debajo del texto). H1 mínimo 36px.
- Contacto: una columna; email puede partir en dos líneas.
- Mobile mock: `reference/Portfolio Mobile.dc.html` (dark/ES y light/EN).

## 6. Accesibilidad

- Contraste: dim sobre bg ≥ 4.5:1 en ambos temas (verificado). Cian como color de texto solo en tamaños ≥ 15px o peso 500.
- Íconos decorativos con `aria-hidden`; toggles con `aria-label` y `aria-pressed`.
- Canvas del hero `aria-hidden`, `pointer-events: none`.

<style>
  /* Full width and its own stacking context: the canvas paints at z-index 0 above the
     fixed aurora, the columns at z-index 1 above the canvas, and no z-index in the hero
     can reach past the section. */
  .hero {
    position: relative;
    isolation: isolate;
  }

  /* The only two-column grid with a 380px floor, and the only block with this vertical
     padding: both appear once in the site, so neither becomes a utility. */
  .columns {
    position: relative;
    z-index: 1;
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 380px), 1fr));
    gap: clamp(32px, 5vw, 72px);
    align-items: center;
    padding-block: clamp(72px, 10vw, 140px) clamp(64px, 8vw, 110px);
  }

  .column {
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    gap: 28px;
    min-width: 0;
  }

  .eyebrow {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 12px;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    color: var(--color-dim);
  }

  .rule {
    flex: none;
    width: 28px;
    height: 1px;
    background: var(--color-accent);
  }

  /* Its own element, so it blinks forever regardless of how far the typing got. */
  .cursor {
    display: inline-block;
    width: 7px;
    height: 12px;
    margin-left: 6px;
    vertical-align: -1px;
    background: var(--color-accent);
  }

  h1 {
    text-wrap: balance;
  }

  /* A one-off alpha pair, so it is mixed here instead of becoming a token (app.css §2).
     The weight is the h1's own, restated: the accent only clears the contrast threshold
     as text at ≥15px or weight ≥500 (`DESIGN_SPEC` §6), and this is the rule that says
     which of the two this one leans on. */
  .accent {
    color: var(--color-accent);
    font-weight: 600;
    text-shadow: 0 0 40px
      light-dark(
        color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-accent) 30%, transparent),
        color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-accent) 45%, transparent)
      );
  }

  .sub {
    max-width: 480px;
  }

  .ctas {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    gap: 12px;
    margin-top: 6px;
  }

  .cta {
    padding: 14px 22px;
    border-radius: 999px;
    font-size: 15px;
    font-weight: 500;
    transition: border-color 0.2s;
  }

  .primary {
    background: var(--color-ink);
    color: var(--color-bg);
  }

  .secondary {
    border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ink) 14%, transparent);
    color: var(--color-ink);
  }

  .secondary:hover {
    border-color: var(--color-accent);
  }

  .stats {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    gap: 12px 24px;
    margin-top: 10px;
    font-size: var(--text-label);
    white-space: nowrap;
    color: var(--color-dim);
  }

  .stats b {
    color: var(--color-ink);
    font-weight: 500;
  }

  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {

content.content:
## 3. Hero — red de nodos (canvas)

Canvas absoluto, `100vw × 100vh`, `mask-image: linear-gradient(180deg,#000 55%,transparent)`, 30–40 fps (`rAF` con throttle 24ms), `dpr ≤ 2`, debajo del contenido (`z-index` menor que `<main>`).

- **84 nodos** sobre un **elipsoide 3D** centrado cerca de la consola (RX = .56W, RY = .48H, RZ = .5·min(W,H)), proyección perspectiva `f = .9·max(W,H)`; escala `sc = f/(f+z)`; profundidad → `z ∈ [.3,1]` controla tamaño y alfa. Rotación global casi nula (`.00003 rad/frame`); cada nodo deriva en su órbita (`dθ ±.0005`, latitud oscila y rebota en ±1.4 rad, `sin` vertical ±9px).
- **Conexiones**: entre nodos a < 150px, alfa `(1-d/150)·.22` (dark) `.28` (light) × min(z).
- **Formación ✳** al cargar: 300→1200ms los nodos convergen (ease in-out cúbico) al asterisco de 6 brazos (R = .26·min(W,H)) centrado en la consola; hold hasta 1900; se disuelve 1900→2800 mientras la consola aparece (2200).
- **Consola como centro**: 4 anclajes en los bordes de la tarjeta (izq 25%, izq 62%, abajo 50%, arriba 30%) se conectan al nodo visible más cercano (< 280px, evitando los que están detrás de la tarjeta). Cada línea nueva del log dispara un **comando**: pulso desde el anclaje izq-62% al nodo más cercano y luego BFS de 3 saltos (`t = -(hop+1)·.55` de desfase, velocidad `.045/frame`, cola de .18). Al llegar, el nodo hace `flash = 1` (anillo que crece hasta 22px, decae ×.93/frame).
- **Cursor**: nodo violeta con glow; atrae nodos a < 200px (fuerza `(1-d/200)·1.4`, decae ×.9); líneas violeta a nodos < 170px; conexiones cercanas suben alfa +.35. El mouse inclina la cámara (`tilt` ±.25 rad, `rot` ±.15).
- **Colapso al scroll**: `collapse = clamp(scrollY / (.75·vh))`; radio ×`(1-.85·collapse)`, rotación ×`(1+5·collapse)`, `globalAlpha = 1-collapse`; los comandos se detienen con `collapse ≥ .6`.
- Mobile: mismo canvas pero N=48 y sin interacción de cursor (touch). Si el rendimiento cae (< 30fps), bajar a 40 nodos.

## 4. Aurora (fondo global)

input.title: 19 · Page container: content-box, so the grid is 1200px like the mock
input.description:
The root cause behind the hero, console and margin complaints. Fix this first: it moves geometry across the whole site.

## The defect

`container-page` in `src/styles/app.css`:

```css
@utility container-page {
  max-width: 1200px;
  margin-inline: auto;
  padding-inline: clamp(20px, 4vw, 48px);
}
```

Tailwind's reset sets `box-sizing: border-box`, so the 1200px cap **includes** the padding. At a 1512px viewport the content box ends up 1104px wide, starting at x=204.

The mock does the opposite — measured on `handoff/reference/Portfolio.dc.html` at 1512×950:

```
MAIN  max-width: 1200px   padding: 48px   box-sizing: content-box
      border box 1296 wide, content 1200 wide, starting at x=156
```

So every section of the site is **96px narrower and 48px further inward** than the design. That is what makes the H1 wrap to five lines instead of four and the console render 48px too narrow.

## Measured, at 1512×950

| | Mock | Ours | With `content-box` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Content column | 1200 | 1104 | **1200** |
| Content starts at x | 156 | 204 | **156** |
| Hero column | 564 | 516 | **564** |
| H1 width | 564 | 516 | **564** |
| H1 height | 296 (4 lines) | 380 (5 lines) | **304 (4 lines)** |
| Console width | ~562 | 509 | **564** |

Verified in the browser by injecting `.container-page { box-sizing: content-box }` and re-measuring — no other change.

## The fix

Add `box-sizing: content-box` to the `container-page` utility. Check the sections that assume the narrower box (project grid, method steps, contact card) still hold at the wider measure, and re-check the ≤720px end where the padding still has to shrink to 20px.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test asserts the built page's content column is 1200px wide at a 1512px viewport, and that it starts at x=156.
- [ ] The hero H1 renders in **four** lines at 1512px, not five.
- [ ] `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` green; the 7 Playwright tests still pass.
- [ ] Lighthouse still ≥ 0.90 on the four categories (the container change moves CLS-relevant geometry).

## Notes

Depends on nothing. **Blocks 20 and 27** — do not start those until this lands.

input.title: 20 · Nav aligned to the page container
input.description:
## The defect

`Nav.astro` carries its own edge padding instead of sharing the page container:

```css
.nav {
  padding-inline: clamp(20px, 4vw, 48px);   /* no max-width, no centering */
}
```

Measured at 1512×950: the brand sits at **x=48** while every section's content starts at **x=156** (x=204 before issue 19). The nav floats 108px outside the page grid, and the right-hand toggles push all the way to x=1512.

## Deliberate deviation from the mock

The mock has the same misalignment (`nav { padding: 14px 48px }`, full width). This issue **improves on it**: the glass bar stays full-bleed, but its *contents* align to the same 1200px column as the rest of the page — the Apple pattern the design leans on (a full-width chrome band over a fixed content grid).

## The fix

Keep `.nav` full width for the glass and the bottom border, and put an inner wrapper on `container-page` that holds brand / links / toggles. Nothing else in the component changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test asserts the nav's brand left edge equals the left edge of a section's `container-page` content, at 1512px and at 1024px.
- [ ] The right-hand toggle's right edge equals the container's right edge.
- [ ] Below 720px, where `container-page` padding drops to 20px, the nav follows and the section links stay hidden.
- [ ] `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` green.

## Notes

**Depends on 19** — the container geometry has to be right before anything is aligned to it.

input.title: 21 · Nav language toggle renders on two lines
input.description: ## The defect The toggle shows `ES` stacked **above** `/ en` instead of side by side. Root cause is a CSS Grid anonymous-item bug in `Nav.astro`: ```astro {lang.toUpperCase()} / {otherLang} ``` ```css .toggle { display: grid; place-items: center; } .lang { white-space: nowrap; } ``` A grid container wraps every stray text run in an **anonymous grid item**. So `ES` and the text ` / en` become two items, and the default `grid-auto-flow: row` puts them on two rows. `white-space: nowrap` cannot help — they are not on the same line to begin with. Measured: `clientHeight` 34px (the fixed height clips it) against `scrollHeight` **36px** — two 18px lines. ## The fix Any of: make `.toggle` an `inline-flex`, set `grid-auto-flow: column`, or wrap the trailing text in its own span and give the grid one column. Keep the 34px pill height and the `place-items: center` behavior for `.theme`, which is a single-child grid and is fine as is. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A test asserts the lang toggle's `scrollHeight` is not greater than its `clientHeight`, on both `/` and `/en`. - [ ] `ES / en` renders on one line; the pill keeps its 34px height and 999px radius. - [ ] The link is still a real `` with `rel="alternate"` — the no-JS translation path of issue 16 must not regress. - [ ] `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` green.

input.title: 22 · Stack: the marquee blows the page open, and 4-5 shorter rows
input.description:
Two things in `Stack.astro`: a bug that breaks the whole page, and a design change on top of it.

## Part 1 — the bug: page-wide horizontal scroll

Measured at 1512×950: `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` is **3588px** against a 1512px viewport. The mock measures 1512 — no overflow at all.

Root cause: `.stack` is a grid whose single implicit column is sized `auto`, so the track resolves to the **max-content** of its widest item. `.rows` contains `.track { width: max-content; flex-wrap: nowrap }`, which is 3100px of chips. `.row { overflow: hidden }` zeroes the automatic *minimum* size but does nothing to the max-content contribution, so the track grows to 3384px and drags the container, the section and the document with it.

Two visible consequences, both reported:

1. **The subtitle sits at the far end of the horizontal scroll.** `header` is a sibling grid item in the same blown track, so its `auto-fit` two-column grid expands to 3384px and column 2 (`stackSub`) starts at **x=1912** — off screen.
2. **The right-hand fade never shows.** The `mask-image` 8%/92% is symmetric and correct, but 92% of a 3384px row is off screen, so only the left blur is ever visible. This is the "no tiene el blur como en la parte izquierda" report — the mask is fine, the width is not.

A third, quieter one: row 3's track measures 3384px — stretched to the blown row rather than its natural max-content — so `translateX(-50%)` no longer lands on the clone boundary and that row shows a seam once per loop.

**The fix**, verified in the browser: `.stack { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) }` takes `scrollWidth` from 3588 to **1512** and puts the subtitle back at x=772.

## Part 2 — 4-5 rows instead of 3

Design change requested by Marcos, and a **deliberate deviation from the handoff**: `DESIGN_SPEC` §7 and `MOTION_SPEC` §10 both specify three rows at 70s / 85s (reverse) / 78s. With 17-18 chips per row each track runs ~3100px, roughly 2× the viewport, so any given technology is off screen most of the time.

Redistribute the same `stack.rows` content from `handoff/content.json` into **4 or 5 rows**, so each track is closer to one viewport wide and the whole stack reads at a glance. Keep: the marquee, the alternating direction, the pause on hover, the symmetric edge mask, the `● USO A DIARIO / ○ TAMBIÉN HABLO` legend and the highlighted-chip rule. Assign speeds per row in the same 70-85s family, and keep the duplicated-half structure so the loop stays seamless.

`content.json` is read-only — the regrouping belongs in the component or in `src/lib/`, not in the handoff.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test asserts `document.documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth` on `/` and `/en`, at 1512px, 1024px and 390px. This is the guard that keeps any future section from doing the same thing.
- [ ] The stack subtitle is inside the viewport, in the header's second column.
- [ ] Each row's `.track` width equals exactly 2× the width of one `.half`, so `translateX(-50%)` is seamless.
- [ ] 4 or 5 rows; every technology from `stack.rows` appears exactly once per half, none dropped.
- [ ] Both edges fade: a test asserts the mask is symmetric and the row is no wider than its container.
- [ ] With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the rows are static, wrapped and fully readable.
- [ ] `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` green.

input.title: 23 · Experience: timeline dot off-center, and "también con" stacks vertically
input.description:
Two defects in `Experience.astro`, same file, one PR.

## 1 — The timeline dot is not centered on the company

```css
.dot { margin-top: 28px; }
```

A magic number that does not track what it should line up with. Measured against the card's top edge, identically on all five jobs:

| | Offset from card top |
|---|---|
| Dot center | 34px |
| Logo center | 49px |

**15px off**, on every entry. The dot should sit on the vertical center of the company row — the 56px logo, which starts after the card's 20px padding, so its center is at 48px.

Fix it so it is derived, not guessed: align the dot to `.who` (the logo + name row) rather than offsetting it from the card by hand, so it survives any change to the card padding or the logo size — including issue 15, when the real logos replace the striped placeholder.

## 2 — "TAMBIÉN CON" renders as a vertical list

`DESIGN_SPEC` §5 puts the company names in a horizontal row inside the dashed box. `.also` is a flex row, but `.also-list` inside it has **no rule at all** — it falls back to `display: block`, so the four names stack. Measured: `display: block`, height 96px for 4 items.

Give `.also-list` `display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap` with a gap in the family of the `.also` box (14px 28px). It should wrap to a second line on narrow viewports rather than overflow.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test asserts, for every job, that the dot's vertical center equals the logo's vertical center within 1px.
- [ ] The assertion is derived from the rendered geometry, not from a hardcoded 48px — it has to keep holding when the logos change.
- [ ] A test asserts `.also-list` lays its items out on one line at 1512px, and that its height is one row's worth.
- [ ] The `.also-list` wraps instead of overflowing at 390px, and issue 22's no-horizontal-scroll guard still passes.
- [ ] `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` green.

## Notes

The `alsoWithCompanies` list in `src/lib/ui.ts` (Creativa Media Lab, Kodai, Hashme, Demedis) is still taken from the mock and **pending Marcos's confirmation**. This issue does not change its contents.

input.title: 24 · Projects: the shimmer cuts off at the right edge and restarts
input.description:
## The defect

The diagonal shimmer over each preview travels, then visibly stops half-visible at the right edge and snaps back to the start. It reads as a cut, not a loop.

`Projects.astro` + `app.css`:

```css
.shimmer { left: -40%; width: 40%; transform: skewX(-12deg); }
.shimmer { animation: shimmer 2.8s ease-in-out infinite; }   /* under no-preference */
@keyframes shimmer { to { transform: translateX(250%); } }
```

The band is 40% of the frame and starts at `left: -40%`, so it is already offscreen-left before any transform. It then travels `translateX(250%)` of its **own** width = 100% of the frame, landing with its left edge at 60% and its **right edge exactly on the frame's right edge**. So the last thing you see is the band parked against the right border — and `ease-in-out` decelerates into precisely that moment — before it teleports back to `-40%`.

`MOTION_SPEC` §9 specifies `translateX(-100% → 250%)`, i.e. the band starts at `left: 0` and is moved offscreen by the transform. With `left: 0`, `translateX(250%)` puts the left edge at 100% of the frame — fully past the right edge, invisible at the moment it wraps. Our `left: -40%` double-counts the initial offset and eats 40% off the end of the travel.

## The fix

Restore the handoff's geometry: `left: 0`, and animate `from { translateX(-100%) } to { translateX(250%) }`. Then confirm the loop actually reads as continuous — with the band fully clear of both edges at the wrap point, the reset is invisible. If a beat between passes is wanted, express it as keyframe percentages (band offscreen from ~70% to 100% of the cycle) rather than leaving the band parked on screen.

`@keyframes shimmer` is shared in `app.css`; check nothing else consumes it before changing it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test asserts the shimmer's bounding box does not intersect the preview frame at either `0%` or `100%` of the animation — the loop point is invisible by construction.
- [ ] The band still enters from the left, is skewed `-12deg`, is 40% wide, and uses `accent@.12`.
- [ ] The animation stays inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` — the whole-site guard in `tests/a11y.test.ts` must still pass.
- [ ] `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` green.

input.title: 25 · Telecentro preview: screenshot /t-play, not the root
input.description:
## The ask

`public/previews/telecentro.com.ar.jpg` is a screenshot of `https://telecentro.com.ar/`. It should be **`https://telecentro.com.ar/t-play`** — the product Marcos actually worked on, and what the card's description claims.

## The constraint

`scripts/capture-previews.ts` navigates to `project.url` straight from `handoff/content.json`:

```ts
await page.goto(project.url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 60_000 })
```

and `content.json` line 176 / 391 has `"url": "https://telecentro.com.ar/"` for both languages. **`handoff/` is read-only** (`CLAUDE.md`), so the URL cannot be edited there.

The card's outgoing link is a separate decision from what gets screenshotted, so they need to stop being the same value. Add a host-keyed shot-URL override next to the existing `PREVIEWS` table in `src/lib/projects.ts` — that file already owns the host-keyed preview policy, and keying by host (never by index) is the rule that survives a reordered `content.json`. `capture-previews.ts` then reads the override and falls back to `project.url`.

Open question for Marcos: should the **card link** also point at `/t-play`, or stay on the root? Defaulting to keeping the link on the root and only changing the screenshot, which is what was asked — say so if you want both.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test asserts the shot URL resolved for `telecentro.com.ar` is `https://telecentro.com.ar/t-play`, and that every other project falls back to its `content.json` URL.
- [ ] The override is keyed by host, and a test asserts reversing `content.es.projects` does not change any resolved shot URL.
- [ ] `bun scripts/capture-previews.ts telecentro.com.ar` regenerates the JPEG; it is committed, still 960×660, quality 82, and the six previews together stay well under the ~723 KB the set weighs today.
- [ ] The new screenshot shows the T-Play product page, not the Telecentro home.
- [ ] `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` green; Lighthouse still ≥ 0.90.

`scripts/capture-previews.ts` navigates to `project.url` straight from `handoff/content.json`:

```ts
await page.goto(project.url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 60_000 })
```

and `content.json` line 176 / 391 has `"url": "https://telecentro.com.ar/"` for both languages. `handoff/` **is read-only** (`CLAUDE.md`), so the URL cannot be edited there.

The card's outgoing link is a separate decision from what gets screenshotted, so they need to stop being the same value. Add a host-keyed shot-URL override next to the existing `PREVIEWS` table in `src/lib/projects.ts` — that file already owns the host-keyed preview policy, and keying by host (never by index) is the rule that survives a reordered `content.json`. `capture-previews.ts` then reads the override and falls back to `project.url`.

input.title: 26 · Aurora: the bottom of the page turns olive-green as you scroll
input.description:
## The defect

Scrolling down, a large soft stain grows behind the content and dominates the contact section and footer. It reads as a stray shadow that came unstuck from the footer. It is not a shadow — it is the aurora.

`src/lib/motion/math.ts`:

```ts
export function auroraStyle(p: number) {
  return {
    filter: `hue-rotate(${Math.round(p * 260)}deg) saturate(${round(1 + 0.4 * p, 3)})`,
    opacity: 0.45 + 0.55 * Math.min(1, p * 2.5),
    translateY: `${round(-12 * p)}vh`,
  }
}
```

Measured at the bottom of the document: `opacity: 1`, `filter: hue-rotate(260deg) saturate(1.4)`, `translateY(-12vh)`.

Two things compound. The opacity ramp reaches **1.0 at only 40% of the document**, so the blobs run at full strength for the entire second half. And `hue-rotate(260deg)` takes the cyan accent (~187°) round to ~87° — yellow-green. Full-strength olive over the last three sections. Confirmed on a screenshot at the footer: the whole upper-right quadrant is a green smear, and the contact card sits on top of it.

## Not a regression — a spec that does not survive contact

`MOTION_SPEC` §4 does specify `hue-rotate(p·260deg)` and `opacity .45 → 1` in the first 40%. This is faithfully implemented; it just looks wrong on the real page, where the mock's short scroll never reached high `p` with this much page below it.

So this is a **design tuning decision, not a bug fix**, and it needs a call rather than a "correct" answer. The options, roughly:

1. Cap the hue sweep so it stays inside the cyan → violet family the palette owns (the design's secondary is violet at ~260°, not green) — e.g. rotate toward violet and stop, instead of a full 260° sweep past green.
2. Flatten the opacity ramp, or ramp it back down over the last stretch so the footer is calm.
3. Both.

Whichever is chosen, the aurora must stay decorative and must not cost contrast: the contact card and the footer sit over it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `auroraStyle` is unit-tested at `p = 0, .2, .4, .7, 1` against the chosen curve — the math lives in `math.ts` and stays testable without a DOM.
- [ ] No hue in the sweep leaves the cyan-violet family (assert the resolved hue range, do not eyeball it).
- [ ] The contact card's text and the footer still meet 4.5:1 with the aurora at its strongest, in both themes.
- [ ] `MOTION_SPEC` §4 is the read-only source of truth, so the deviation is recorded in `docs/superpowers/specs/` with the reason, not silently applied.
- [ ] `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` green; Lighthouse accessibility does not drop.

input.title: 27 · Hero fidelity: height, console and node cloud against the mock
input.description:
The leftovers of the hero comparison once issue 19 has landed. **Do not start this before 19 is merged** — the container fix already closes most of the gap, and measuring against the old geometry would send this in the wrong direction.

## What 19 already fixes

Verified by injecting `box-sizing: content-box` and re-measuring at 1512×950:

| | Mock | Before | After 19 |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 width | 564 | 516 | 564 |
| H1 height | 296 (4 lines) | 380 (5 lines) | 304 (4 lines) |
| Console width | ~562 | 509 | 564 |

So "el título se estira mucho para abajo" and "la terminal se ve muy pequeña" are both consequences of the container, not of the hero.

## What is left after that

Re-measure all of it against `handoff/reference/Portfolio.dc.html` at 1512×950 before writing any code — the numbers below are from the pre-19 build and are a starting point, not the target.

1. **Hero height.** Ours is 994px against the mock's 909px. The stats row (`8+ años · 5 empresas · 6 plataformas`) is cut by the fold at 950px; in the mock it clears it with room to spare. Check the `padding-block: clamp(72px,10vw,140px) clamp(64px,8vw,110px)` against the mock's actual padding, and check whether the 28px column gap is the mock's.

2. **The node cloud sits too low.** The mock spreads the nodes across the full hero with the density around the console's center at y≈530; ours weight to the bottom, with bright nodes still visible at y=850-950 where the mock's are nearly gone. `MOTION_SPEC` §3 puts the `mask-image: linear-gradient(180deg,#000 55%,transparent)` on the canvas — check whether it is actually taking effect and whether the extra 85px of hero height is what pushes `cloudCenter` down. The ellipsoid math in `math.ts` (`rx = .56w, ry = .48h, rz = .5·min(w,h)`) matches the spec and is unit-tested; suspect the inputs, not the formula.

3. **Formation timing.** A screenshot at 2.5s catches the ✳ formation mid-dissolve (spec: dissolves 1900→2800ms) as a dense cluster of large rings over the H1. Confirm that is the intended read of that beat and that it does not sit on top of the headline — at 7s the cloud settles and matches the mock much more closely.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Issue 19 is merged first.
- [ ] The hero's total height is within 5% of the mock's at 1512×950, and the stats row is above the fold at a 950px viewport height.
- [ ] A test asserts the node cloud's vertical center tracks the console's center, so it cannot drift again when the hero is re-measured.
- [ ] The canvas mask is asserted to be applied — node alpha below 55% of the canvas height is measurably lower than above it.
- [ ] Reduced motion still mounts no canvas (the existing Playwright test), and the hero reads without JavaScript.
- [ ] `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` green; Lighthouse still ≥ 0.90.

{"id":"PV3-24","uuid":"e5dd72a4-14dd-4067-a4e0-1221bbcfcc22","title":"19 · Page container: content-box, so the grid is 1200px like the mock","description":"The root cause behind the hero, console and margin complaints. Fix this first: it moves geometry across the whole site.

## The defect

`container-page` in `src/styles/app.css`:

```css
@utility container-page {
  max-width: 1200px;
  margin-inline: auto;
  padding-inline: clamp(20px, 4vw, 48px);
}
```

Tailwind's reset sets `box-sizing: border-box`, so the 1200px cap **includes** the padding. At a 1512px viewport the content box ends up 1104px wide, starting at x=204.

The mock does the opposite — measured on `handoff/reference/Portfolio.dc.html` at 1512×950:

```
MAIN  max-width: 1200px   padding: 48px   box-sizing: content-box
      border box 1296 wide, content 1200 wide, starting at x=156
```
