content.text:
Nueve issues creados en Linear. Todo medido contra el mock renderizado (`handoff/reference/Portfolio.dc.html`) a 1512×950, no a ojo.

**El hallazgo que cambia el plan:** cuatro de tus quejas son el mismo bug.

`container-page` usa `max-width: 1200px` con `box-sizing: border-box` (el reset de Tailwind), así que el padding de 48px va **adentro** del tope. El mock usa `content-box`. Resultado: todo el sitio es 96px más angosto y arranca 48px más adentro que el diseño.

| | Mock | Nuestro | Con `content-box` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Columna de contenido | 1200 | 1104 | **1200** |
| Columna del hero | 564 | 516 | **564** |
| H1 | 296px (4 líneas) | 380px (5 líneas) | **304px (4 líneas)** |
| Consola | ~562 | 509 | **564** |

Lo verifiqué inyectando una sola línea de CSS. El título estirado y la terminal chica se arreglan solos.

**El otro root cause:** `.stack` es un grid cuya columna implícita se dimensiona al `max-content` de la marquesina. `document.scrollWidth` da **3588px** contra un viewport de 1512 (el mock: 1512). De ahí salen tres síntomas: el scroll horizontal, el subtítulo a x=1912 (fuera de pantalla), y el blur derecho que nunca ves — la máscara es simétrica (8%/92%), pero el 92% de 3384px está fuera de la pantalla. `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)` lo lleva de 3588 a 1512.

**Los issues**

| | Bloquea | |
|---|---|---|
| [PV3-24](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-24) | **19** · Container `content-box` | Urgent — bloquea 20 y 27 |
| [PV3-27](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-27) | **22** · Stack: overflow + 4-5 filas | Urgent |
| [PV3-25](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-25) | **20** · Nav alineado al container | ← 19 |
| [PV3-26](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-26) | **21** · Toggle de idioma en dos líneas | |
| [PV3-28](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-28) | **23** · Timeline dot + "también con" | |
| [PV3-29](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-29) | **24** · Shimmer se corta | |
| [PV3-30](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-30) | **25** · Telecentro `/t-play` | |
| [PV3-31](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-31) | **26** · Aurora verde oliva | |
| [PV3-32](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-32) | **27** · Fidelidad del hero | ← 19 |

**Causas exactas de los demás:**

- **Toggle de idioma**: `.toggle` es `display: grid` y el texto suelto ` / en` se convierte en un *anonymous grid item* → segunda fila. `nowrap` no puede ayudar, no están en la misma línea. Medido: `scrollHeight` 36 vs `clientHeight` 34.
- **Dot del timeline**: `margin-top: 28px` a dedo. Centro del dot a 34px del tope de la card, centro del logo a 49px. 15px de error en las cinco.
- **"También con" vertical**: `.also-list` no tiene *ninguna* regla CSS, cae a `display: block`.
- **Shimmer**: `left: -40%` + `translateX(250%)` termina con el borde derecho de la banda justo sobre el borde del frame — y `ease-in-out` desacelera exactamente ahí. El handoff dice `left: 0` y `-100% → 250%`, que la deja fuera de pantalla al saltar.
- **La "sombra que crece" no es una sombra**: es la aurora. `hue-rotate(p·260deg)` lleva el cian (~187°) a ~87° = verde oliva, y el opacity llega a 1.0 al 40% del documento. Se ve en el screenshot del footer.

**Dos cosas necesitan tu decisión, están anotadas en los issues:**

1. El handoff especifica **3 filas** en el stack (`DESIGN_SPEC` §7). Vos pedís 4-5. Lo escribí como desvío deliberado del handoff.
2. Lo mismo con la aurora: `MOTION_SPEC` §4 especifica ese `hue-rotate` de 260°. Está implementado fiel — se ve mal igual. El issue plantea las opciones (cortar el barrido en violeta, aplanar el opacity, o ambas) en vez de elegir por vos.

Y una pregunta suelta: el **link** de la card de Telecentro, ¿va también a `/t-play` o queda en la raíz? Por defecto dejé solo el screenshot, que es lo que pediste.

Nada de esto está codeado — solo issues. PR #17 sigue mergeable y sin tocar. ¿Arrancamos por la 19, que destraba las otras dos?

{"id":"PV3-30","uuid":"7b9a8f88-f3fd-4e04-9b3f-9e1e7f4ab0a5","title":"25 · Telecentro preview: screenshot /t-play, not the root","description":"## The ask

`public/previews/telecentro.com.ar.jpg` is a screenshot of `https://telecentro.com.ar/`. It should be `https://telecentro.com.ar/t-play` — the product Marcos actually worked on, and what the card's description claims.

## The constraint

`scripts/capture-previews.ts` navigates to `project.url` straight from `handoff/content.json`:

```ts
await page.goto(project.url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 60_000 })
```

and `content.json` line 176 / 391 has `"url": "https://telecentro.com.ar/"` for both languages. `handoff/` **is read-only** (`CLAUDE.md`), so the URL cannot be edited there.

The card's outgoing link is a separate decision from what gets screenshotted, so they need to stop being the same value. Add a host-keyed shot-URL override next to the existing `PREVIEWS` table in `src/lib/projects.ts` — that file already owns the host-keyed preview policy, and keying by host (never by index) is the rule that survives a reordered `content.json`. `capture-previews.ts` then reads the override and falls back to `project.url`.

**Decided (Marcos, 2026-09-06): the card link goes to** `/t-play` **too.** So the override replaces the URL for both uses — the screenshot and the outgoing `href` — and `content.json` stays untouched.

- [ ] The override is keyed by host, and a test asserts reversing `content.es.projects` does not change any resolved shot URL.
- [ ] `bun scripts/capture-previews.ts telecentro.com.ar` regenerates the JPEG; it is committed, still 960×660, quality 82, and the six previews together stay well under the ~723 KB the set weighs today.
- [ ] The new screenshot shows the T-Play product page, not the Telecentro home.
- [ ] `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` green; Lighthouse still ≥ 0.90.","priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-30/25-telecentro-preview-screenshot-t-play-not-the-root","gitBranchName":"marcosarrietadev/pv3-30-25-telecentro-preview-screenshot-t-play-not-the-root","createdAt":"2026-09-06T22:28:44.572Z","updatedAt":"2026-09-06T22:32:19.270Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Marcos Arrieta","createdById":"bb0a2931-8847-4417-a560-93afc144566f","team":"Portfolio-djmaam-v3","teamId":"d7096bbd-61ad-4ded-940b-6ad9d53f03d5"}

# 17 · Playwright smoke + Lighthouse CI — spec

Issue: [PV3-22](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-22) · Branch: `feat/17-e2e-lighthouse`
Design: design doc §6, §9 · `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §13

## Goal

The end-to-end safety net, plus the performance budget. Small on purpose: 304 unit tests
already cover every formula, so this block only has to prove the DOM plumbing runs in a
real browser.

## Context

`bun test` covers content, i18n, all the motion math, contrast and the a11y invariants.
None of it opens a browser. Every block so far verified its own DOM work by running
shipped scripts against hand-written stubs — which is honest, but not the same as a
browser.

Two things are still unverified for exactly that reason:

- Whether the focus ring is **visually unclipped**. `overflow: hidden` on `.row`,
  `.preview` and `.edge` could crop a 2px offset ring on an element sitting flush
  against them. Issue 16 flagged this and could not close it.
- Whether the frame budget holds on a throttled machine rather than an M4.

CI today runs lint, test and build on Bun 1.4.0.

## Scope

### 1. Playwright

`bun add -d @playwright/test`. This is the one dependency this block adds, and it is
justified: nothing else drives a real browser.

`playwright.config.ts`: Chromium only, `webServer` running `bun run preview` against the
static build, `baseURL` from it, retries 0 locally and 1 in CI, trace on first retry.

### 2. The six smoke tests — `e2e/smoke.spec.ts`

Each asserts something a unit test structurally cannot:

1. **The hero boots.** After the boot sequence, the `h1` and all five `[data-boot]`
   elements are at opacity 1. Guards the whole `boot.ts` timeline in a real event loop.
2. **The theme toggle round-trips.** Click, assert `documentElement.dataset.theme` and
   `style.colorScheme` both flipped, reload, assert it persisted.
3. **The language toggle navigates.** Click, land on `/en`, assert `<html lang="en">` and
   that the `h1` matches `content.en.h1a`.
4. **A reveal fires on scroll.** A card below the fold starts at opacity 0 and reaches 1
   after scrolling to it.
5. **The method sticky advances.** Scroll through the 280vh track and assert the active
   step index goes 0 → 4 and the indicator text tracks it.
6. **`reduce` mounts no canvas.** With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` emulated:
   `page.locator('canvas')` has count 0, and the hero text is visible from the first
   frame.

Plus the one issue 16 could not do:

7. **The focus ring is not clipped.** Tab to each interactive element and assert its
   `getBoundingClientRect`, expanded by the 2px ring and its 2px offset, is inside the
   client rect of every `overflow: hidden` ancestor. If an element fails, fix the CSS —
   do not delete the assertion.

Keep it at these seven. A large E2E suite is slow and flaky, and this one exists to catch
what unit tests cannot reach, not to re-cover them.

### 3. Lighthouse CI

`bun add -d @lhci/cli`. Mobile preset against the static build.

Thresholds, all **error** level: Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices and SEO each
≥ 90.

If Performance misses, degrade in the order `MOTION_SPEC` §13 fixes — shimmer, then
aurora, then node count — and **write down in the PR what was degraded and the before/after
numbers**. Do not lower the threshold, and do not degrade preemptively: measure first.

### 4. CI wiring

Extend `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: the existing `check` job stays as is, and a second job
runs the build once, then Playwright and Lighthouse against it. Cache the Playwright
browser download.

Total CI time must stay under 5 minutes. Report the actual number.

### 5. Scripts

Add `test:e2e` (`playwright test`) and `test:lh` (`lhci autorun`). `tests/scaffold.test.ts`
asserts the exact set of package scripts, so it needs updating — that is expected, not a
reason to avoid adding them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The seven Playwright tests pass locally three runs in a row with no flake.
- [ ] They pass in CI.
- [ ] Lighthouse reports ≥ 90 on all four categories, mobile, against the built site.
- [ ] The focus-ring test genuinely fails when a ring is clipped — prove it by temporarily narrowing an ancestor, then revert.
- [ ] `bun run lint`, `bun test` and `bun run build` still pass; the scaffold script test is updated.
- [ ] Total CI wall time under 5 minutes.

## Out of scope

Visual regression snapshots. Cross-browser runs — Chromium only; the design targets
evergreen browsers and a second engine doubles CI time for little here. Deploy (issue 18).

# 19 · Page container: content-box — spec

Issue: [PV3-24](https://linear.app/portfolio-djmaam-v3/issue/PV3-24) · Branch: `feat/19-page-container`
Design: `handoff/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §2 · `handoff/reference/Portfolio.dc.html`

## Goal

Make the page grid 1200px wide, as the design says it is. Today it is 1104px, and that
one number is what makes the hero H1 wrap to five lines instead of four and the console
render 48px too narrow.

## Context

`DESIGN_SPEC` §2 says: `max-width: 1200px; padding: 0 clamp(20px, 4vw, 48px)`. Our
`container-page` implements it literally:

```css
@utility container-page {
  max-width: 1200px;
  margin-inline: auto;
  padding-inline: clamp(20px, 4vw, 48px);
}
```

But Tailwind's reset sets `box-sizing: border-box`, so the 1200px cap **includes** the
padding. The mock does the opposite — measured on `handoff/reference/Portfolio.dc.html`
in Chromium at 1512×950:

```
MAIN   max-width: 1200px   padding: 48px   box-sizing: content-box
       border box 1296 wide, content box 1200 wide, starting at x=156
```

So the spec line is ambiguous and we read it the wrong way. Every section of the site is
96px narrower and 48px further inward than the design intends.

`box-sizing` only affects an explicit `width`/`max-width`, so this changes nothing below
a 1296px viewport: with `width: auto` the content box is still the parent minus the
padding, exactly as today. The whole change lands above 1296px.

## Measured

At 1512×950, Chromium, dark:

|  | Mock | Ours | Ours with `content-box` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Content column | 1200 | 1104 | **1200** |
| Content starts at x | 156 | 204 | **156** |
| Hero column | 564 | 516 | **564** |
| H1 width | 564 | 516 | **564** |
| H1 height | 296 (4 lines) | 380 (5 lines) | **304 (4 lines)** |
| Console width | ~562 | 509 | **564** |

The "ours with content-box" column was produced by injecting the single declaration into
the live page and re-measuring. Nothing else changed.

## Scope

### 1. The change

Add `box-sizing: content-box` to the `container-page` utility. That is the whole fix.

### 2. What has to be re-checked, not assumed

Nine call sites consume `container-page`. Widening the content box by 96px can change how
their `auto-fit` grids resolve, and two of them have code that depends on the answer:

- **Projects** — `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 300px), 1fr))` with `gap: 14px`.
  Four columns need `4×300 + 3×14 = 1242px`, so 1200px still resolves to three. It clears
  by 42px, which is close enough that `projectDelay(i) = 90 * (i % 3)` in
  `src/lib/projects.ts` — which hardcodes three columns — would silently stagger the wrong
  cards if it ever tipped. Assert the column count, so it cannot tip unnoticed.
- **Method** — the pin decision is `inner.offsetHeight + 64 <= vh` at runtime. A wider
  container makes the five steps shorter, so the section pins at viewport heights where it
  used to stay in flow. Confirm it still both pins and unpins, and that the 0 → 4 advance
  still works.
- **Contact, About, Experience, Stack, Hero, Footer** — visual only; no code reads their
  width.

### 3. The regression guard

The reason this survived sixteen blocks is that nothing measures page geometry: every
existing test reads source or the built CSS. Add `e2e/layout.spec.ts` with the geometry
assertions below — a small file that owns "the page grid is the right size and in the
right place", so the next section to get this wrong fails in CI.

Keep it to layout invariants. It is not a visual regression suite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At a 1512px viewport, on `/` and `/en`, the content box of `container-page` measures
      1200px and starts at x=156 — asserted against the mock's numbers, not ours.
- [ ] At 1280px and 390px the container still measures viewport minus twice the resolved
      padding, so nothing regresses below the cap.
- [ ] The hero H1 renders in **four** lines at 1512px. Asserted by measuring its height
      against its `line-height`, not by counting words.
- [ ] The projects grid resolves to exactly three columns at 1512px, so `projectDelay`
      keeps matching the layout.
- [ ] The method section still pins and still advances 0 → 4 (the existing Playwright test
      covers the advance; confirm the pin decision at the new width).
- [ ] `bun run build`, `bun test`, `bun run lint` and the Playwright suite all pass.
- [ ] Lighthouse stays ≥ 0.90 on all four categories on both routes.

## Out of scope

Aligning the nav to this container — that is issue 20, and it depends on this landing
first. Re-measuring the hero's height, node cloud and console against the mock — issue 27,
same dependency. The stack's horizontal overflow is issue 22 and is a separate root cause;
it is not fixed or worked around here.
SPEC

1	import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'
2	
3	/**
4	 * The page grid (spec 19). Every other test of this repo reads source or the built CSS;
5	 * none of them measures anything. That is exactly why `container-page` shipped 96px
6	 * narrower than the design for sixteen blocks — a stylesheet that says `max-width: 1200px`
7	 * reads correct, and only a layout engine can say whether the content box is 1200 or 1104.
8	 *
9	 * The numbers below come from the mock — `handoff/reference/Portfolio.dc.html` rendered
10	 * in Chromium at 1512×950 — not from our own output, so they cannot drift toward whatever
11	 * we happen to ship.
12	 */
13	
14	/** `DESIGN_SPEC` §2: `max-width: 1200px; padding: 0 clamp(20px, 4vw, 48px)`. */
15	const CONTENT = 1200
16	const MAX_PAD = 48
17	const MIN_PAD = 20
18	
19	/** The mock's own geometry at a 1512px viewport: content 1200 wide, starting at x=156. */
20	const WIDE = { viewport: 1512, content: CONTENT, left: (1512 - CONTENT) / 2 }
21	
22	const ROUTES = ['/', '/en']
23	
24	/** The content box of the first `container-page` on the page, and where it starts. */
25	const measure = (page: import('@playwright/test').Page) =>
26	  page.evaluate(() => {
27	    const el = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.container-page')
28	    if (!el) throw new Error('no .container-page on the page')
29	    const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect()
30	    const style = getComputedStyle(el)
31	    const padLeft = parseFloat(style.paddingLeft)
32	    const padRight = parseFloat(style.paddingRight)
33	    return {
34	      content: rect.width - padLeft - padRight,
35	      left: rect.left + padLeft,
36	      right: rect.right - padRight,
37	      padLeft,
38	      padRight,
39	      boxSizing: style.boxSizing,
40	    }
41	  })
42	
43	for (const route of ROUTES) {
44	  test(`${route} lays its content out on the mock's 1200px grid`, async ({ page }) => {
45	    await page.setViewportSize({ width: WIDE.viewport, height: 950 })
46	    await page.goto(route)
47	
48	    const box = await measure(page)
49	    expect(box.content).toBeCloseTo(WIDE.content, 0)
50	    expect(box.left).toBeCloseTo(WIDE.left, 0)
51	    // The padding is still there — the cap moved, the gutter did not.
52	    expect(box.padLeft).toBeCloseTo(MAX_PAD, 0)
53	    expect(box.padRight).toBeCloseTo(MAX_PAD, 0)
54	  })
55	
56	  test(`${route} keeps every container on the same grid`, async ({ page }) => {
57	    await page.setViewportSize({ width: WIDE.viewport, height: 950 })
58	    await page.goto(route)
59	
60	    // One misaligned section is the bug class this file exists for, and the first
61	    // container agreeing with the mock says nothing about the other eight.
62	    const edges = await page.evaluate(() =>
63	      [...document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.container-page')].map((el) => {
64	        const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect()
65	        const style = getComputedStyle(el)
66	        return {
67	          left: Math.round(rect.left + parseFloat(style.paddingLeft)),
68	          width: Math.round(
69	            rect.width - parseFloat(style.paddingLeft) - parseFloat(style.paddingRight),
70	          ),
71	        }
72	      }),
73	    )
74	
75	    expect(edges.length).toBeGreaterThan(5)
76	    for (const edge of edges) {
77	      expect(edge).toEqual({ left: WIDE.left, width: WIDE.content })
78	    }
79	  })
80	}
81	
82	test('below the cap the container is the viewport minus its gutters', async ({ page }) => {
83	  // `box-sizing` only touches an explicit `max-width`, so nothing here may move: with
84	  // `width: auto` the content box has always been the parent minus the padding. This is
85	  // the assertion that says the fix changed only what it was meant to change.
86	  for (const [width, pad] of [
87	    [1280, MAX_PAD],
88	    [390, MIN_PAD],
89	  ] as const) {
90	    await page.setViewportSize({ width, height: 950 })
91	    await page.goto('/')
92	
93	    const box = await measure(page)
94	    expect(box.padLeft).toBeCloseTo(pad, 0)
95	    expect(box.content).toBeCloseTo(width - 2 * pad, 0)
96	    expect(box.left).toBeCloseTo(pad, 0)
97	  }
98	})
99	
100	test('the hero H1 renders in four lines, like the mock', async ({ page }) => {
101	  await page.setViewportSize({ width: WIDE.viewport, height: 950 })
102	  await page.goto('/')
103	
104	  // Measured against its own line-height rather than by counting words, so the assertion
105	  // survives a copy change and is the same test in both languages.
106	  const lines = await page.evaluate(() => {
107	    const h1 = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.hero h1')!
108	    return h1.getBoundingClientRect().height / parseFloat(getComputedStyle(h1).lineHeight)
109	  })
110	
111	  expect(Math.round(lines)).toBe(4)
112	})
113	
114	test('the projects grid stays at three columns, which is what projectDelay assumes', async ({
115	  page,
116	}) => {
117	  await page.setViewportSize({ width: WIDE.viewport, height: 950 })
118	  await page.goto('/')
119	
120	  // `projectDelay(i) = 90 * (i % 3)` hardcodes three. Four columns need 4×300 + 3×14 =
121	  // 1242px and the grid now has 1200, so it clears by 42 — close enough that it has to
122	  // be asserted rather than reasoned about.
123	  const columns = await page.evaluate(() => {
124	    const grid = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.cards')!
125	    return getComputedStyle(grid).gridTemplateColumns.split(/\s+/).length
126	  })
127	
128	  expect(columns).toBe(3)
129	})

Closes PV3-24. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/19-page-container.md`.

## The bug

`DESIGN_SPEC` §2 says `max-width: 1200px; padding: 0 clamp(20px, 4vw, 48px)`. That line is ambiguous, and Tailwind's `border-box` reset resolved it the wrong way — the 1200px cap swallowed the 48px gutters, so the content column shipped at **1104px**.

The mock is `content-box`: 1200 of content inside a 1296 border box, starting at x=156. Measured on `handoff/reference/Portfolio.dc.html` in Chromium at 1512×950.

## Measured, 1512×950

| | Mock | Before | After |

You are executing Linear issue PV3-27 in the portfolio-v3 repo (Astro 7 static + Bun + TypeScript strict + Tailwind v4, no UI framework).

FIRST: read `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root and follow it exactly. Everything you write — code, comments, identifiers, commit messages, test names, the spec — is **American English**. `handoff/` is READ-ONLY, never edit it.

## Your block: `22-stack`

Two things in `src/components/Stack.astro`: a bug that breaks the whole page, and a design change on top of it.

### Part 1 — the bug: page-wide horizontal scroll

Measured at 1512×950: `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` is **3588px** against a 1512px viewport. The design mock (`handoff/reference/Portfolio.dc.html`, which renders standalone in Chromium — open it with a `file://` URL) measures 1512. No overflow at all.

Root cause: `.stack` is a grid whose single implicit column is sized `auto`, so the track resolves to the **max-content** of its widest item. `.rows` contains `.track { width: max-content; flex-wrap: nowrap }`, which is 3100px of chips. `.row { overflow: hidden }` zeroes the automatic *minimum* size but does nothing to the max-content contribution, so the track grows to 3384px and drags the container, the section and the document with it.

Three visible consequences, all reported by the site's owner:

1. **The subtitle sits at the far end of the horizontal scroll.** `header` is a sibling grid item in the same blown track, so its `auto-fit` two-column grid expands to 3384px and column 2 (`stackSub`) starts at x=1912 — off screen.
2. **The right-hand fade never shows.** The `mask-image` 8%/92% is symmetric and correct, but 92% of a 3384px row is off screen, so only the left blur is ever visible. The mask is fine; the width is not.
3. Row 3's track measures 3384px — stretched to the blown row rather than its natural max-content — so `translateX(-50%)` no longer lands on the clone boundary and that row shows a seam once per loop.

I already verified the fix in a live browser: `.stack { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) }` takes `scrollWidth` from 3588 to **1512** and puts the subtitle back at x=772. Confirm this yourself rather than trusting me, and satisfy yourself it is the right fix rather than the first one that moved the number.

### Part 2 — 4 or 5 rows instead of 3

Requested by the site's owner, and a **deliberate deviation from the handoff**: `handoff/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §7 and `handoff/MOTION_SPEC.md` §10 both specify three rows at 70s / 85s (reverse) / 78s. With 17-18 chips per row each track runs ~3100px, roughly 2× the viewport, so any given technology is off screen most of the time.

Redistribute the same `stack.rows` content from `handoff/content.json` into **4 or 5 rows** — you choose which, and justify it in the spec from the measured track widths — so each track is closer to one viewport wide and the whole stack reads at a glance.

Keep: the marquee, the alternating direction, the pause on hover, the symmetric edge mask, the `● USO A DIARIO / ○ TAMBIÉN HABLO` legend, and the highlighted-chip rule (`stack.core` decides, and the component reads membership from that single list — do not introduce a second list). Assign per-row speeds in the same 70-85s family.

`content.json` is read-only, so the regrouping belongs in the component or in `src/lib/`. Prefer a small pure function in `src/lib/` if the grouping has any logic worth testing without a DOM — this repo keeps math in pure functions precisely so `bun test` covers it.

Because this deviates from a read-only spec, **record the deviation and the reason in your spec file**. Do not apply it silently.

1. `git checkout -b feat/22-stack` from `main`.
2. Write `docs/superpowers/specs/22-stack.md` BEFORE any code. Follow the shape of `docs/superpowers/specs/19-page-container.md` — read it, it is the most recent and closest model. Commit the spec on its own (`docs: spec for 22 stack`).
3. Then TDD: failing assertions FIRST, watch them fail, then fix. A test you never saw fail is not a test.

## Acceptance criteria

Below its 1296px cap, +`width: auto` makes an unconstrained box resolve to the same thing a capped one does, so +`.nav`'s own clamp happens to land on the same numbers as `container-page`'s by +coincidence — the two formulas are identical. Above the cap, `container-page` stops +growing and `.nav` does not, and the nav drifts away from every section under it. + +The mock has the same bug (`handoff/reference/Portfolio.dc.html`: `nav { padding: 14px +48px }`, full width, no cap). This is a deliberate improvement over the mock, decided by +the site's owner: the glass bar stays full-bleed for its background and bottom border, +but its *contents* — brand, links, toggles — align to the same 1200px column as the rest +of the page. A full-width chrome band over a fixed content grid, the Apple pattern the +design leans on elsewhere. + +### Measured + +Chromium, dark, `/`: + +| Viewport | | Nav content edge | `container-page` edge | Drift | +| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | +| 1512px | brand left | 48 | 156 | **108px** | +| 1512px | theme toggle right | 1464 | 1356 | **108px** | +| 1024px | brand left | 40.95 | 40.96 | 0 (below the cap, the formulas agree) | + +At 1512px the nav's contents sit 108px outside the grid on both sides — the two clamp +formulas agree everywhere under 1296px and diverge everywhere above it, which is exactly +`container-page`'s own cap behavior (spec 19). + +### Fix + +Keep `.nav` full width for the glass background and the border. **Bloque 20 listo — PR #19** (`feat/20-nav-align`), cierra PV3-25 y PV3-26. Revisé el diff yo mismo, no me quedé con el reporte.

| | Antes | Después |
|---|---|---|
| Brand, borde izquierdo | 48 | **156** (= container) |
| Toggle tema, borde derecho | 1464 | **1356** (= container) |
| Toggle idioma | 2 líneas (scrollH 36 / clientH 32) | **1 línea** |

El fix del toggle terminó siendo **una sola propiedad**: `.toggle` de `grid` a `flex`. Flex no crea anonymous items en filas separadas, así que `ES / en` queda en línea, y `.theme` — que tiene un solo hijo — sigue centrado igual. Más limpio que las alternativas que había anotado en el issue.

Para el nav: `.nav` queda full-bleed (glass + borde) y un `.inner.container-page` adentro lleva brand/links/toggles. Buen detalle del agente: notó que a diferencia del `.inner` de Method, este es block child y no flex item, así que no necesita repetir la fórmula de ancho — `max-width` + `margin auto` alcanzan.

Gates: 310 unit tests (5 nuevos), lint, build, 22 e2e (8 nuevos). Los tests los vio fallar primero contra el código roto, reproduciendo los 108px de drift. CI corriendo.

**Branch** `feat/22-stack` · **PR** https://github.com/djmaam/portfolio-v3/pull/21 (closes PV3-27)

**Root cause** — `.stack`'s implicit grid column was `auto`, sized to the max-content of its widest item; `.row { overflow: hidden }` zeroes the automatic *minimum* size but not the max-content contribution, so the 3384px marquee track sized the column, the container and the document. **Before → after** (Chromium 1512×950, both routes identical; the mock measures 1512 with no overflow):
- `documentElement.scrollWidth` 3540 → **1512**
- `.stack` / `.row` width 3384 → **1200**

**Four rows, not five** — measured from the chips (34px + 7.2px/char, 52 chips = 4728px) against the 1200px content column: 3 rows = 1.24-1.41× the column (a row never fits), 4 rows = 0.96-1.01× (a half *is* the column, so the viewport holds one full pass), 5 rows = 0.74-0.81× (half narrower than the column, so both copies are on screen and the same chip shows twice — reads as a bug). Regrouping is `groupRows` in `src/lib/stack.ts` from the same read-only `stack.rows`; `stack.core` is still the only highlight list. Deviation from `DESIGN_SPEC` §3.7 / `MOTION_SPEC` §10 recorded in the spec and the PR body. Speeds 70 / 85 reverse / 78 / 82 reverse.

**Gates** — `bun test` 311 pass / 0 fail (was 305). `bun run lint` clean. `bun run build` clean. `PORT=4402 bun run test:e2e` 21 passed. Lighthouse deliberately not run locally.

**Two things you should know, not green-on-red:**
1. The 390px document assertion does **not** pass — but not because of the stack. `Footer.astro`'s ASCIImoji stacks 15 hidden faces in one inline-grid cell; at 390 the cell is squeezed to 84px while its widest face is ~111px, so the document measures 397 (ES) / 391 (EN) while every section fits. Pre-existing, previously masked by the stack's own 3404px, and `Footer.astro` is outside my file list — so I did not edit it. It ships as a `test.fail` with the cause written down (turns red when fixed, rather than silently skipped), and the section-level 390 assertion is strict and passes. One-line fix for the footer owner: `overflow: hidden` on `.moji`.
2. The reported row-3 seam did not reproduce: on `main` all three tracks already measured exactly 2× their halves (3384 = 2×1692). The row was stretched; the track was not. The two defects that did reproduce are the document overflow and the off-screen subtitle.

content.text:
Dos bloques más, y cerré una cosa que había quedado a medias.

**Bloque 22 — PR #21** (`feat/22-stack`), cierra PV3-27.

| | Antes | Después |
|---|---|---|
| `scrollWidth` del documento | 3540 | **1512** |
| Ancho de `.stack` / `.row` | 3384 | **1200** |
| Subtítulo del stack | x=1864 (fuera) | **x=772** |
| Filas | 3 | **4** |
| Halves | 1550/1485/1692 | **1182/1207/1193/1146** |

Eligió 4 filas midiendo, no a ojo: con 3 cada half es 1.24-1.41× la columna de 1200 (nunca entra una fila completa); con 5 es 0.74-0.81× — **las dos copias quedan en pantalla y el mismo chip aparece dos veces**, que se lee como bug. Con 4, cada half ≈ la columna. Buen razonamiento, no se me había ocurrido el problema del duplicado visible.

**Me equivoqué en un punto del issue.** Escribí que la fila 3 tenía un seam por track estirado. No reproduce: en `main` los tres tracks ya medían exactamente 2× sus halves (3384 = 2×1692). La fila estaba estirada, el track no — inferí el seam de la medición de la fila sin verificar los halves.

**Y algo que el agente reportó en vez de tapar:** la guarda de 390px la dejó como `test.fail` porque fallaba por un bug **preexistente del footer**, fuera de sus archivos. Lo verifiqué y era cierto: `.moji` se comprimía a 84px contra una cara de 111px, y las 15 caras ocultas (`visibility: hidden` igual ocupa layout) empujaban 7px fuera del viewport. La última pérdida horizontal del sitio, tapada hasta ahora por los 3384px del stack.

Lo cerré yo en esa misma rama. **No** con `overflow: hidden` como sugería — eso clipearía la cara visible, que es justo lo que el truco de apilar caras existe para evitar. `flex: none` mantiene el ancho y hace que envuelva la línea de firma. Ahora `scrollWidth` 390 = `clientWidth` en ambas rutas, y la guarda asserta a 390 sin condiciones.

**Bloque 24 — PR #22** (`feat/24-projects`), cierra PV3-29 y PV3-30.

El shimmer tenía **un segundo bug que no vi**: `.shimmer` llevaba `transform: skewX(-12deg)` estático y el keyframe `to` era `translateX(250%)` a secas. Un keyframe reemplaza el transform entero, así que el skew se iba interpolando hasta desaparecer en cada ciclo. Ahora los dos van en ambos keyframes.

Y una corrección a mi propio issue: pedí volver al `-100% → 250%` literal del `MOTION_SPEC`. El agente midió que el skew convierte la banda en un paralelogramo cuyo bounding box real es ~28px más ancho que su ancho de layout, así que con los números exactos del spec la esquina sesgada seguía tocando el frame en el punto de loop. Usó `-120% → 270%`. Lo verificó de dos formas, incluyendo muestrear el transform computado cada 200ms durante dos ciclos.

Telecentro: `URL_OVERRIDES` keyed por host junto a `PREVIEWS`, y el `href` de la card y el `goto` del script de captura resuelven por la misma función, así que no pueden divergir. El screenshot nuevo es correcto — "Telecentro Play / Ahora tenemos T-Play para todos" — y pesa 66 KB contra 208 KB del anterior; el set completo bajó a 596 KB.

CI verde en **#19** y **#20**. Corriendo en **#21** y **#22**. Falta solo Hero (27).

content.text:
CI verde en **#21** y **#22**.

Un detalle que vale la pena: el commit anterior de la 22 — el que llevaba el `test.fail` del footer — **falló en CI**. En el runner de Linux las fuentes fallback de los ASCIImoji miden distinto, así que en una ruta el overflow no ocurría, el test pasaba, y un `test.fail()` que pasa se reporta como fallo. Era flaky por construcción. Cerrar el bug del footer en vez de marcarlo resultó ser lo correcto por una razón más dura que el gusto: el marcador no sobrevivía a CI. Con el fix, ambas rutas asertan a 390 sin condiciones y el run pasa.

**Estado: cuatro PRs verdes, listos para mergear.**

| PR | Bloque | Cierra |
|---|---|---|
| [#19](https://github.com/djmaam/portfolio-v3/pull/19) | 20 · Nav: alineación + toggle idioma | PV3-25, PV3-26 |
| [#20](https://github.com/djmaam/portfolio-v3/pull/20) | 23 · Experience: dot + "también con" | PV3-28 |
| [#21](https://github.com/djmaam/portfolio-v3/pull/21) | 22 · Stack: overflow + 4 filas (+ footer) | PV3-27 |
| [#22](https://github.com/djmaam/portfolio-v3/pull/22) | 24 · Projects: shimmer + Telecentro | PV3-29, PV3-30 |

Los cuatro salieron de `main` en paralelo. **#21 toca `e2e/layout.spec.ts` y `Footer.astro`; #22 toca `@keyframes shimmer` en `app.css`** — regiones distintas, pero si mergeás en cualquier orden y alguno da conflicto, avisame y lo resuelvo.

Falta solo Hero (27), que sigue corriendo — es la más larga porque tiene que medir el mock antes de tocar nada.

content.text:
Los cuatro mergeados. Corrí las gates sobre `main` combinado — que es lo que nadie había hecho, cada rama estaba verde en aislamiento.

**324 unit tests · 39 e2e · lint · build · Lighthouse `1.00 / 0.96 / 1.00 / 1.00` en ambas rutas.** `scrollWidth` 1512 = `clientWidth`. Sin conflictos entre las cuatro.

En el screenshot del stack se ve el resultado: 4 filas que entran, subtítulo en su columna, blur en los dos bordes, y los toggles del nav alineados al margen de la página.

**Pero salta a la vista la 26.** Mirá el fondo — todo el bloque de proyectos y stack está bañado en verde oliva, y en la sección de Método se ve el barrido pasando por marrón/naranja. Es el `hue-rotate(p·260deg)` de la aurora llevando el cian a ~87°, sumado al opacity que llega a 1.0 al 40% del documento. Es lo que describiste como "una sombra que va creciendo".

Necesito tu decisión para arrancarla:

1. **Cortar el barrido de hue** — que rote de cian hacia violeta (el secundario que la paleta ya tiene) y frene ahí, sin pasar por verde.
2. **Aplanar la rampa de opacity** — que no llegue a 1.0, o que baje sobre el final para que el footer quede tranquilo.
3. **Las dos.**

Mi recomendación es la **3**, con el peso en la 1: el verde no está en la paleta del diseño en ningún lado, así que aunque bajes el opacity seguís teniendo un color que no es tuyo, solo más tenue. Y una vez que el barrido queda dentro de cian→violeta, dejar algo de rampa de opacity conserva la intención del `MOTION_SPEC` §4 de que la página "se encienda" al scrollear.

Hero (27) sigue corriendo — es la más larga porque mide el mock antes de tocar nada. Te aviso cuando termine.
